items.stem: A ceramic capacitive pressure transducer consists of parallel conducting plates of overlapping area 0.24 m² separated by a uniform alumina ceramic layer of thickness 2.50 × 10⁻⁴ m and relative permittivity 3.8. A steady potential difference of 150 V is maintained across the plates (ε₀ = 8.85 × 10⁻¹² F m⁻¹). What electrostatic energy is stored in the capacitor?

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates C = εᵣε₀A/d and U = ½CV² to obtain 3.63 × 10⁻⁴ J (D).

items.stem: Parallel rectangular plates of area 0.6 m² in a aerospace humidity-compensated sensor enclose a solid polyimide sheet slab (relative permittivity 5.2) that sets the plate separation at 8.00 × 10⁻⁴ m. Taking ε₀ = 8.85 × 10⁻¹² F m⁻¹ with an applied terminal voltage of 320 V, calculate the capacitance of the dielectric-filled assembly.

markScheme.criterion: Applies C = εᵣε₀A / d to obtain 3.45 × 10⁻⁸ F (A).

items.stem: A laboratory prototype of a high-voltage laser flashlamp cell employs parallel electrodes of area 0.9 m², a cast epoxy resin dielectric of thickness 5.00 × 10⁻⁴ m and relative permittivity 6.8, and a charging supply of 150 V (ε₀ = 8.85 × 10⁻¹² F m⁻¹). What magnitude of charge is stored on each conducting plate?
items.workedSolution: Capacitance C = εᵣε₀A / d = 1.08 × 10⁻⁷ F. Plate charge Q = CV = 1.08 × 10⁻⁷ × 150 = 1.62 × 10⁻⁵ C.

markScheme.criterion: Combines C = εᵣε₀A/d with Q = CV to obtain 1.62 × 10⁻⁵ C (D).

options.distractorRationale: Ignores the dielectric polarization factor εᵣ when computing capacitance before Q = CV.

items.stem: During a dielectric bench test, a silicone elastomer sheet with relative permittivity 3.2 completely fills the 3.00 × 10⁻⁴ m gap between parallel metal plates of area 1.5 m² inside a industrial proximity-sensing pad. When the assembly is charged to 320 V (take ε₀ = 8.85 × 10⁻¹² F m⁻¹), calculate the energy stored per unit volume inside the dielectric.
items.workedSolution: Uniform field E = V / d = 320 / 0.0003 = 1.07 × 10⁶ V m⁻¹. Energy density u_E = ½εᵣε₀E² = 0.5 × 3.2 × 8.85 × 10⁻¹² × (1.07 × 10⁶)² = 16.1 J m⁻³.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates E = V/d and u_E = ½εᵣε₀E² to obtain 16.1 J m⁻³ (B).

items.stem: An engineer calibrates a precision touch-panel sensing element built from parallel plates of area 0.48 m² separated by 2.00 × 10⁻⁴ m of borosilicate glass whose relative permittivity is 4.4. With 150 V connected steadily between the plates and ε₀ = 8.85 × 10⁻¹² F m⁻¹, What electrostatic energy is stored in the capacitor?

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates C = εᵣε₀A/d and U = ½CV² to obtain 1.05 × 10⁻³ J (A).

items.stem: In a laboratory dielectric-constant cell, a regulated DC supply applies 150 V across two flat parallel electrodes of effective area 1.5 m² spaced 4.00 × 10⁻⁴ m apart. The space between the electrodes is filled uniformly by nylon spacer of relative permittivity 7.5 (ε₀ = 8.85 × 10⁻¹² F m⁻¹). What magnitude of charge is stored on each conducting plate?
items.workedSolution: Capacitance C = εᵣε₀A / d = 2.49 × 10⁻⁷ F. Plate charge Q = CV = 2.49 × 10⁻⁷ × 150 = 3.73 × 10⁻⁵ C.

markScheme.criterion: Combines C = εᵣε₀A/d with Q = CV to obtain 3.73 × 10⁻⁵ C (D).

items.stem: Within a polymer-film pulse energy storage cell, a uniform electric field is established across a 2.50 × 10⁻⁴ m layer of polypropylene film (εᵣ = 3.8) sandwiched between conducting plates of area 0.4 m² held at a potential difference of 320 V. Using ε₀ = 8.85 × 10⁻¹² F m⁻¹, calculate the energy stored per unit volume inside the dielectric.
items.workedSolution: Uniform field E = V / d = 320 / 0.00025 = 1.28 × 10⁶ V m⁻¹. Energy density u_E = ½εᵣε₀E² = 0.5 × 3.8 × 8.85 × 10⁻¹² × (1.28 × 10⁶)² = 27.5 J m⁻³.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates E = V/d and u_E = ½εᵣε₀E² to obtain 27.5 J m⁻³ (A).

items.stem: A medical defibrillator test capacitor consists of parallel conducting plates of overlapping area 0.75 m² separated by a uniform mica insulator layer of thickness 8.00 × 10⁻⁴ m and relative permittivity 5.2. A steady potential difference of 150 V is maintained across the plates (ε₀ = 8.85 × 10⁻¹² F m⁻¹). What electrostatic energy is stored in the capacitor?

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates C = εᵣε₀A/d and U = ½CV² to obtain 4.85 × 10⁻⁴ J (A).

items.stem: Parallel rectangular plates of area 1.25 m² in a microbalance displacement detector enclose a solid fused quartz wafer slab (relative permittivity 6.8) that sets the plate separation at 5.00 × 10⁻⁴ m. Taking ε₀ = 8.85 × 10⁻¹² F m⁻¹ with an applied terminal voltage of 320 V, calculate the capacitance of the dielectric-filled assembly.

markScheme.criterion: Applies C = εᵣε₀A / d to obtain 1.50 × 10⁻⁷ F (D).

items.stem: A laboratory prototype of a ceramic capacitive pressure transducer employs parallel electrodes of area 0.32 m², a alumina ceramic dielectric of thickness 3.00 × 10⁻⁴ m and relative permittivity 3.2, and a charging supply of 150 V (ε₀ = 8.85 × 10⁻¹² F m⁻¹). What magnitude of charge is stored on each conducting plate?
items.workedSolution: Capacitance C = εᵣε₀A / d = 3.02 × 10⁻⁸ F. Plate charge Q = CV = 3.02 × 10⁻⁸ × 150 = 4.53 × 10⁻⁶ C.

markScheme.criterion: Combines C = εᵣε₀A/d with Q = CV to obtain 4.53 × 10⁻⁶ C (C).

items.stem: During a dielectric bench test, a polyimide sheet sheet with relative permittivity 4.4 completely fills the 2.00 × 10⁻⁴ m gap between parallel metal plates of area 0.6 m² inside a aerospace humidity-compensated sensor. When the assembly is charged to 320 V (take ε₀ = 8.85 × 10⁻¹² F m⁻¹), calculate the energy stored per unit volume inside the dielectric.
items.workedSolution: Uniform field E = V / d = 320 / 0.0002 = 1.60 × 10⁶ V m⁻¹. Energy density u_E = ½εᵣε₀E² = 0.5 × 4.4 × 8.85 × 10⁻¹² × (1.60 × 10⁶)² = 49.8 J m⁻³.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates E = V/d and u_E = ½εᵣε₀E² to obtain 49.8 J m⁻³ (C).

items.stem: An engineer calibrates a high-voltage laser flashlamp cell built from parallel plates of area 0.9 m² separated by 6.00 × 10⁻⁴ m of cast epoxy resin whose relative permittivity is 6. With 150 V connected steadily between the plates and ε₀ = 8.85 × 10⁻¹² F m⁻¹, What electrostatic energy is stored in the capacitor?
items.workedSolution: Capacitance C = εᵣε₀A / d = 6 × 8.85 × 10⁻¹² × 0.9 / 0.0006 = 7.97 × 10⁻⁸ F. Stored energy U = ½CV² = 0.5 × 7.97 × 10⁻⁸ × (150)² = 8.96 × 10⁻⁴ J.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates C = εᵣε₀A/d and U = ½CV² to obtain 8.96 × 10⁻⁴ J (B).

items.stem: In a capacitive MEMS accelerometer, parallel plates of area 0.25 m² separated by 3.00 × 10⁻⁴ m with dielectric relative permittivity 4.8 are initially charged to 100 V (take ε₀ = 8.85 × 10⁻¹² F m⁻¹). The capacitor is disconnected from the DC source so the plates remain electrically isolated, and the plate separation is then adjusted to 1.50 × 10⁻⁴ m (maintaining relative permittivity 4.8). What is the final electrostatic energy stored in the modified state?
items.workedSolution: Initial capacitance C = 3.54 × 10⁻⁸ F, modified capacitance C′ = 7.08 × 10⁻⁸ F. Under isolated-charge, final stored energy U′ = 8.85 × 10⁻⁵ J.

markScheme.criterion: Computes modified capacitance C′ and evaluates final stored energy 8.85 × 10⁻⁵ J (B).

items.stem: A variable-gap precision electrometer has plate area 0.45 m², initial separation 6.00 × 10⁻⁴ m, and relative permittivity 6.5, energised initially at 220 V (ε₀ = 8.85 × 10⁻¹² F m⁻¹). Next, the assembly is kept connected across the DC source at constant potential difference while the plate separation is adjusted to 9.00 × 10⁻⁴ m with εᵣ = 6.5 throughout. What is the final electrostatic energy stored in the modified state?
items.workedSolution: Initial capacitance C = 4.31 × 10⁻⁸ F, modified capacitance C′ = 2.88 × 10⁻⁸ F. Under constant-voltage, final stored energy U′ = 6.96 × 10⁻⁴ J.

markScheme.criterion: Computes modified capacitance C′ and evaluates final stored energy 6.96 × 10⁻⁴ J (C).

items.stem: During calibration of a dielectric displacement gauge (ε₀ = 8.85 × 10⁻¹² F m⁻¹), a 420 V supply charges parallel electrodes of area 0.7 m² spaced 4.00 × 10⁻⁴ m apart with relative permittivity 4. The electrodes are disconnected from the DC source so the plates remain electrically isolated, and the plate separation is then adjusted to 8.00 × 10⁻⁴ m at unchanged relative permittivity 4. What is the signed change in stored electrostatic energy ΔU = U_final − U_initial?
items.workedSolution: Initial C = 6.19 × 10⁻⁸ F and U_i = ½CV² = 5.46 × 10⁻³ J. Modified C′ = 3.10 × 10⁻⁸ F gives U_f = 0.0109 J, so ΔU = U_f − U_i = 5.46 × 10⁻³ J.

markScheme.criterion: Determines U_i and U_f under the isolated-charge constraint to obtain ΔU = 5.46 × 10⁻³ J (B).

items.stem: Parallel electrodes of area 1 m² in a electrostatic actuator test rig enclose a medium of relative permittivity 5.5 across an initial gap of 2.40 × 10⁻⁴ m at 180 V (ε₀ = 8.85 × 10⁻¹² F m⁻¹). Subsequently, the device is kept connected across the DC source at constant potential difference while the plate separation is adjusted to 6.00 × 10⁻⁴ m with the same εᵣ = 5.5. What is the final electrostatic energy stored in the modified state?
items.workedSolution: Initial capacitance C = 2.03 × 10⁻⁷ F, modified capacitance C′ = 8.11 × 10⁻⁸ F. Under constant-voltage, final stored energy U′ = 1.31 × 10⁻³ J.

markScheme.criterion: Computes modified capacitance C′ and evaluates final stored energy 1.31 × 10⁻³ J (D).

items.stem: An experimental parallel-plate laboratory condenser features plates of area 0.35 m² at initial spacing 5.00 × 10⁻⁴ m filled with a medium of relative permittivity 3.5 and charged to 350 V (take ε₀ = 8.85 × 10⁻¹² F m⁻¹). The plates are disconnected from the DC source so the plates remain electrically isolated, and the plate separation is then adjusted to 2.50 × 10⁻⁴ m while εᵣ stays at 3.5. What is the new potential difference across the isolated plates?
items.workedSolution: For isolated plates, charge Q is conserved while C′ = C₀(d/d′). Therefore V′ = Q / C′ = V₀(d′/d) = 350 × (0.00025 / 0.0005) = 175 V.

markScheme.criterion: Uses charge conservation V′ = V₀(d′/d) to obtain 175 V (D).

items.stem: Charged initially to 140 V, a vacuum-insulated capacitive load cell with plate area 0.55 m², gap 3.00 × 10⁻⁴ m, and relative permittivity 4.8 is kept connected across the DC source at constant potential difference while the plate separation is adjusted to 4.50 × 10⁻⁴ m (εᵣ = 4.8, ε₀ = 8.85 × 10⁻¹² F m⁻¹). What is the signed change in stored electrostatic energy ΔU = U_final − U_initial?
items.workedSolution: Initial C = 7.79 × 10⁻⁸ F and U_i = ½CV² = 7.63 × 10⁻⁴ J. Modified C′ = 5.19 × 10⁻⁸ F gives U_f = 5.09 × 10⁻⁴ J, so ΔU = U_f − U_i = −2.54 × 10⁻⁴ J.

markScheme.criterion: Determines U_i and U_f under the constant-voltage constraint to obtain ΔU = −2.54 × 10⁻⁴ J (A).

items.stem: In a high-voltage plate-separation apparatus, parallel plates of area 0.85 m² separated by 6.00 × 10⁻⁴ m with dielectric relative permittivity 6.5 are initially charged to 280 V (take ε₀ = 8.85 × 10⁻¹² F m⁻¹). The capacitor is disconnected from the DC source so the plates remain electrically isolated, and the plate separation is then adjusted to 0.0012 m (maintaining relative permittivity 6.5). What is the final electrostatic energy stored in the modified state?
items.workedSolution: Initial capacitance C = 8.15 × 10⁻⁸ F, modified capacitance C′ = 4.07 × 10⁻⁸ F. Under isolated-charge, final stored energy U′ = 6.39 × 10⁻³ J.

markScheme.criterion: Computes modified capacitance C′ and evaluates final stored energy 6.39 × 10⁻³ J (D).

items.stem: A piezo-positioned capacitor stage has plate area 0.25 m², initial separation 4.00 × 10⁻⁴ m, and relative permittivity 4, energised initially at 100 V (ε₀ = 8.85 × 10⁻¹² F m⁻¹). Next, the assembly is kept connected across the DC source at constant potential difference while the plate separation is adjusted to 0.001 m with εᵣ = 4 throughout. What is the final electrostatic energy stored in the modified state?
items.workedSolution: Initial capacitance C = 2.21 × 10⁻⁸ F, modified capacitance C′ = 8.85 × 10⁻⁹ F. Under constant-voltage, final stored energy U′ = 4.42 × 10⁻⁵ J.

markScheme.criterion: Computes modified capacitance C′ and evaluates final stored energy 4.42 × 10⁻⁵ J (D).

items.stem: During calibration of a capacitive MEMS accelerometer (ε₀ = 8.85 × 10⁻¹² F m⁻¹), a 220 V supply charges parallel electrodes of area 0.45 m² spaced 2.40 × 10⁻⁴ m apart with relative permittivity 5.5. The electrodes are disconnected from the DC source so the plates remain electrically isolated, and the plate separation is then adjusted to 1.20 × 10⁻⁴ m at unchanged relative permittivity 5.5. What is the signed change in stored electrostatic energy ΔU = U_final − U_initial?
items.workedSolution: Initial C = 9.13 × 10⁻⁸ F and U_i = ½CV² = 2.21 × 10⁻³ J. Modified C′ = 1.83 × 10⁻⁷ F gives U_f = 1.10 × 10⁻³ J, so ΔU = U_f − U_i = −1.10 × 10⁻³ J.

markScheme.criterion: Determines U_i and U_f under the isolated-charge constraint to obtain ΔU = −1.10 × 10⁻³ J (A).

items.stem: Parallel electrodes of area 0.7 m² in a variable-gap precision electrometer enclose a medium of relative permittivity 3.5 across an initial gap of 5.00 × 10⁻⁴ m at 420 V (ε₀ = 8.85 × 10⁻¹² F m⁻¹). Subsequently, the device is kept connected across the DC source at constant potential difference while the plate separation is adjusted to 7.50 × 10⁻⁴ m with the same εᵣ = 3.5. What is the final electrostatic energy stored in the modified state?
items.workedSolution: Initial capacitance C = 4.34 × 10⁻⁸ F, modified capacitance C′ = 2.89 × 10⁻⁸ F. Under constant-voltage, final stored energy U′ = 2.55 × 10⁻³ J.

markScheme.criterion: Computes modified capacitance C′ and evaluates final stored energy 2.55 × 10⁻³ J (A).

items.stem: An experimental dielectric displacement gauge features plates of area 1 m² at initial spacing 3.00 × 10⁻⁴ m filled with a medium of relative permittivity 4.8 and charged to 180 V (take ε₀ = 8.85 × 10⁻¹² F m⁻¹). The plates are disconnected from the DC source so the plates remain electrically isolated, and the plate separation is then adjusted to 6.00 × 10⁻⁴ m while εᵣ stays at 4.8. What is the new potential difference across the isolated plates?
items.workedSolution: For isolated plates, charge Q is conserved while C′ = C₀(d/d′). Therefore V′ = Q / C′ = V₀(d′/d) = 180 × (0.0006 / 0.0003) = 360 V.

markScheme.criterion: Uses charge conservation V′ = V₀(d′/d) to obtain 360 V (B).

items.stem: Charged initially to 350 V, a electrostatic actuator test rig with plate area 0.35 m², gap 6.00 × 10⁻⁴ m, and relative permittivity 6.5 is kept connected across the DC source at constant potential difference while the plate separation is adjusted to 0.0015 m (εᵣ = 6.5, ε₀ = 8.85 × 10⁻¹² F m⁻¹). What is the signed change in stored electrostatic energy ΔU = U_final − U_initial?
items.workedSolution: Initial C = 3.36 × 10⁻⁸ F and U_i = ½CV² = 2.06 × 10⁻³ J. Modified C′ = 1.34 × 10⁻⁸ F gives U_f = 8.22 × 10⁻⁴ J, so ΔU = U_f − U_i = −1.23 × 10⁻³ J.

markScheme.criterion: Determines U_i and U_f under the constant-voltage constraint to obtain ΔU = −1.23 × 10⁻³ J (D).

items.stem: In a parallel-plate laboratory condenser, parallel plates of area 0.55 m² separated by 4.00 × 10⁻⁴ m with dielectric relative permittivity 4 are initially charged to 140 V (take ε₀ = 8.85 × 10⁻¹² F m⁻¹). The capacitor is disconnected from the DC source so the plates remain electrically isolated, and the plate separation is then adjusted to 2.00 × 10⁻⁴ m (maintaining relative permittivity 4). What is the final electrostatic energy stored in the modified state?
items.workedSolution: Initial capacitance C = 4.87 × 10⁻⁸ F, modified capacitance C′ = 9.74 × 10⁻⁸ F. Under isolated-charge, final stored energy U′ = 2.39 × 10⁻⁴ J.

markScheme.criterion: Computes modified capacitance C′ and evaluates final stored energy 2.39 × 10⁻⁴ J (B).

items.stem: In a camera strobe flash bank, two initially uncharged capacitors of capacitances C₁ = 12 μF and C₂ = 24 μF are connected in series across a 11 V DC source. What is the total equivalent capacitance of the series pair?
items.workedSolution: For series capacitors, 1/C_eq = 1/C₁ + 1/C₂, giving C_eq = (12 × 24)/(12 + 24) μF = 8.00 × 10⁻⁶ F.

items.stem: A pulsed-power laboratory network uses a capacitor C_s = 30 μF connected in series with a parallel bank formed by C_p1 = 10 μF and C_p2 = 20 μF across a 19 V DC supply. What is the equivalent capacitance of the complete three-capacitor network?
items.workedSolution: Parallel bank C_p = 10 + 20 = 30 μF. Combining in series with C_s = 30 μF gives C_eq = (C_s C_p)/(C_s + C_p) = 1.50 × 10⁻⁵ F.

markScheme.criterion: Finds C_p = 30 μF and combines in series with C_s to obtain 1.50 × 10⁻⁵ F (B).

items.stem: A 31 V DC power supply energises a series combination of capacitor C₁ = 15 μF and capacitor C₂ = 30 μF inside a avionics backup energy module. What potential difference is developed across capacitor C₁?
items.workedSolution: Equivalent capacitance C_eq = 1.00 × 10⁻⁵ F, so series charge Q = C_eq V₀ = 3.10 × 10⁻⁴ C. Across C₁, V₁ = Q / C₁ = 20.7 V.

markScheme.criterion: Finds common series charge Q and computes V₁ = Q/C₁ = 20.7 V (A).

items.stem: Across a 7 V DC bus in a audio crossover filter module, capacitor C_s (40 μF) lies in series with the parallel combination of C_p1 (15 μF) and C_p2 (25 μF). What total electrostatic energy is stored in the complete network?
items.workedSolution: Parallel bank C_p = 40 μF; total C_eq = 2.00 × 10⁻⁵ F. Stored energy U = ½C_eq V₀² = 0.5 × 2.00 × 10⁻⁵ × (7)² = 4.90 × 10⁻⁴ J.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates C_eq and computes U = ½C_eq V₀² = 4.90 × 10⁻⁴ J (A).

items.stem: Two capacitors rated C₁ = 20 μF and C₂ = 60 μF are wired end-to-end in series across an ideal 17 V terminal supply on a solar inverter buffer stage. What total electrostatic energy is stored in the two-capacitor series combination?
items.workedSolution: C_eq = (C₁C₂)/(C₁ + C₂) = 1.50 × 10⁻⁵ F. Total stored energy U = ½C_eq V₀² = 0.5 × 1.50 × 10⁻⁵ × (17)² = 2.17 × 10⁻³ J.

markScheme.criterion: Determines C_eq and computes U = ½C_eq V₀² = 2.17 × 10⁻³ J (D).

items.stem: In a biomedical amplifier coupling network, parallel branches containing C_p1 = 12 μF and C_p2 = 18 μF are wired in series with capacitor C_s = 60 μF and charged by a steady 29 V source. What is the equivalent capacitance of the complete three-capacitor network?
items.workedSolution: Parallel bank C_p = 12 + 18 = 30 μF. Combining in series with C_s = 60 μF gives C_eq = (C_s C_p)/(C_s + C_p) = 2.00 × 10⁻⁵ F.

markScheme.criterion: Finds C_p = 30 μF and combines in series with C_s to obtain 2.00 × 10⁻⁵ F (C).

items.stem: During testing of a DC rail smoothing subcircuit, an engineer connects uncharged capacitors C₁ = 18 μF and C₂ = 36 μF in series with a steady 43 V cell. What is the total equivalent capacitance of the series pair?
items.workedSolution: For series capacitors, 1/C_eq = 1/C₁ + 1/C₂, giving C_eq = (18 × 36)/(18 + 36) μF = 1.20 × 10⁻⁵ F.

items.stem: Across a regulated 23 V rail in a camera strobe flash bank, capacitor C₁ (24 μF) is placed in series with capacitor C₂ (48 μF). What potential difference is developed across capacitor C₁?
items.workedSolution: Equivalent capacitance C_eq = 1.60 × 10⁻⁵ F, so series charge Q = C_eq V₀ = 3.68 × 10⁻⁴ C. Across C₁, V₁ = Q / C₁ = 15.3 V.

markScheme.criterion: Finds common series charge Q and computes V₁ = Q/C₁ = 15.3 V (B).

items.stem: A pulsed-power laboratory network uses a capacitor C_s = 36 μF connected in series with a parallel bank formed by C_p1 = 12 μF and C_p2 = 24 μF across a 37 V DC supply. What is the equivalent capacitance of the complete three-capacitor network?
items.workedSolution: Parallel bank C_p = 12 + 24 = 36 μF. Combining in series with C_s = 36 μF gives C_eq = (C_s C_p)/(C_s + C_p) = 1.80 × 10⁻⁵ F.

markScheme.criterion: Finds C_p = 36 μF and combines in series with C_s to obtain 1.80 × 10⁻⁵ F (A).

items.stem: In a avionics backup energy module, two initially uncharged capacitors of capacitances C₁ = 16 μF and C₂ = 48 μF are connected in series across a 11 V DC source. What total electrostatic energy is stored in the two-capacitor series combination?
items.workedSolution: C_eq = (C₁C₂)/(C₁ + C₂) = 1.20 × 10⁻⁵ F. Total stored energy U = ½C_eq V₀² = 0.5 × 1.20 × 10⁻⁵ × (11)² = 7.26 × 10⁻⁴ J.

markScheme.criterion: Determines C_eq and computes U = ½C_eq V₀² = 7.26 × 10⁻⁴ J (C).

items.stem: A 31 V DC power supply energises a series combination of capacitor C₁ = 30 μF and capacitor C₂ = 90 μF inside a solar inverter buffer stage. What is the total equivalent capacitance of the series pair?
items.workedSolution: For series capacitors, 1/C_eq = 1/C₁ + 1/C₂, giving C_eq = (30 × 90)/(30 + 90) μF = 2.25 × 10⁻⁵ F.

items.stem: In a switched-capacitor sample-and-hold stage, capacitor C₁ = 10 μF is charged to V₁ = 23 V, isolated from its supply, and then connected via switch S in parallel with capacitor C₂ = 30 μF (initially uncharged). What final common potential difference is established across both capacitors?
items.workedSolution: Total conserved charge Q_net = C₁V₁ + C₂V₂ = 2.30 × 10⁻⁴ C. Final parallel capacitance C_eq = 40 μF, so V_f = Q_net / (C₁ + C₂) = 5.75 V.

items.stem: During a charge-conservation test on a isolated laboratory capacitor bank, C₁ = 15 μF at initial voltage V₁ = 47 V is connected by closing switch S across C₂ = 45 μF (initially uncharged). What final common potential difference is established across both capacitors?

items.stem: In a heart-pacemaker timing circuit, a 20 μF capacitor initially charged to 6 V begins discharging through a 2.5 kΩ resistor when switch S closes, and a sensor samples the circuit after 0.02 s. What is the potential difference across the capacitor at t = 0.02 s?
items.workedSolution: Time constant τ = RC = 0.0500 s. For discharging, V_C(0.02 s) = 6 e^(−0.02/0.0500) = 4.02 V.

markScheme.criterion: Finds τ = RC and evaluates V_C at t = 0.02 s to obtain 4.02 V (A).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Assumes the capacitor reaches or retains the full supply voltage V₀ instantaneously.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Applies the charging equation V₀(1 − e^(−t/RC)) instead of exponential discharge V₀e^(−t/RC).

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Divides elapsed time t by half-time RC ln 2 instead of the RC time constant τ = RC in the exponent.

items.stem: An uncharged 50 μF capacitor in a camera shutter delay module is connected at switch closure in series with a 5 kΩ resistor across an ideal 12 V DC source and observed after 0.125 s. What is the half-time t_{1/2} required for the exponential transient to decay by half?

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Reports the RC time constant τ = RC (36.8% decay time) instead of multiplying by ln 2 for 50% decay.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Divides RC by ln 2 instead of multiplying RC by ln 2.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Multiplies RC by 0.500 (assuming linear decay) instead of ln 2 ≈ 0.693.

items.stem: During a oscilloscope RC time-constant practical test, switch S connects a pre-charged 120 μF capacitor (initial p.d. 18 V) across a 10 kΩ fixed resistor for an elapsed interval of 1.08 s. What is the current in the resistor at t = 1.08 s?
items.workedSolution: Initial current I₀ = V₀ / R = 18 / 10000 = 1.80 × 10⁻³ A. With τ = RC = 1.20 s, I(t) = I₀ e^(−t/τ) = 7.32 × 10⁻⁴ A.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Stops at the initial peak current I₀ = V₀/R without applying exponential decay e^(−t/RC).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Uses (V₀/R)(1 − e^(−t/RC)), mistakenly thinking RC current grows toward V₀/R instead of decaying exponentially from V₀/R.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Substitutes resistance in kΩ instead of Ω when computing V₀/R.

items.stem: Within a industrial watchdog reset timer, a 30 V DC rail charges an initially uncharged 25 μF capacitor via a 20 kΩ series resistor; the transient is evaluated at 0.6 s. How much electrostatic energy is stored in the capacitor at t = 0.6 s?
items.workedSolution: τ = RC = 0.500 s, giving V_C(0.6 s) = 21.0 V. Stored energy U = ½CV_C² = 0.5 × 2.50 × 10⁻⁵ × (21.0)² = 5.49 × 10⁻³ J.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates V_C(t) and computes U(t) = ½CV_C(t)² = 5.49 × 10⁻³ J (C).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Forgets the factor of one-half in U(t) = ½CV_C(t)².

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Scales stored energy linearly with V_C(t)/V₀ instead of quadratically with (V_C(t)/V₀)² in U = ½CV_C².

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Introduces an extraneous factor of one-half during algebraic rearrangement.

items.stem: A rotary position-sensing pickup winding has 300 turns, cross-sectional area 0.02 m², and total loop resistance 5 Ω. Uniform magnetic field lines make an angle of 35° with the plane of the coil while the flux density ramps uniformly from 0.22 T to 0.55 T over 0.025 s. What is the initial magnetic flux linkage NΦ₁ of the coil?
items.workedSolution: Angle to coil normal θ_n = 55°. Initial flux linkage NΦ₁ = NBA cos θ_n = 300 × 0.22 × 0.02 × cos 55° = 0.757 Wb.

markScheme.criterion: Uses θ_normal = 55° in NΦ₁ = NBA cos θ_normal to obtain 0.757 Wb (A).

items.stem: A ballistic galvanometer flip-coil of 75 turns, area 0.004 m², and total circuit resistance 5 Ω sits perpendicular to a uniform magnetic field that reverses from B₁ = +0.12 T to B₂ = −0.120 T in 0.04 s. What total magnitude of electric charge ΔQ flows around the circuit during this reversal?
items.workedSolution: Signed field change |ΔB| = |-0.12 − 0.12| = 0.24 T, so |Δ(NΦ)| = 75 × 0.24 × 0.004 = 0.0720 Wb. Induced charge ΔQ = |Δ(NΦ)| / R = 0.0144 C.

markScheme.criterion: Accounts for field sign reversal in |Δ(NΦ)| and evaluates ΔQ = |Δ(NΦ)|/R = 0.0144 C (A).

items.stem: On a electromagnetic rail-braking demonstrator, a conducting bar of internal resistance 0.4 Ω slides to the left at a steady speed of 4 m s⁻¹ along parallel horizontal rails of negligible resistance spaced 0.2 m apart. A uniform 0.25 T magnetic field (directed into the page) threads the rails, which are bridged by a 1.4 Ω load resistor. What external pulling force magnitude is needed to maintain this constant speed?
items.workedSolution: Motional emf ε = BLv = 0.200 V. Total loop resistance R_tot = 1.4 + 0.4 = 1.8 Ω, giving I = ε / R_tot = 0.111 A. Pulling force F = BIL = 5.56 × 10⁻³ N.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates ε = BLv, I = ε/(R + r), and F = BIL = 5.56 × 10⁻³ N (C).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Neglects the internal resistance of the moving rod and divides by the external load resistance R alone.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Stops after evaluating the induced loop current I = BLv/(R + r) without multiplying by B L.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Computes mechanical input power P = Fv instead of the applied pulling force F.

items.stem: A uniform 0.6 T magnetic field directed out of the page permeates a linear regenerator test track whose smooth conducting rails sit 0.32 m apart across a 2.4 Ω external resistor. An external agent pulls a rod of resistance 0.6 Ω to the right at constant speed 8 m s⁻¹. What is the terminal potential difference across the external load resistor?
items.workedSolution: ε = BLv = 1.54 V; loop current I = ε / (R + r) = 0.512 A. Terminal p.d. across load V_term = I R = 0.512 × 2.4 = 1.23 V.

markScheme.criterion: Uses V_term = BLv × R/(R + r) to obtain 1.23 V (A).

items.stem: In a magnetohydrodynamic copper-bar carriage, parallel rails of separation 0.5 m are closed by a 4.2 Ω resistor inside a perpendicular 1.1 T magnetic field (directed into the page). A metal rod of resistance 0.8 Ω moves steadily to the right at 4 m s⁻¹. What mechanical power must be supplied to keep the rod moving at constant speed?
items.workedSolution: ε = BLv = 2.20 V; R_tot = 4.2 + 0.8 = 5 Ω. Mechanical input power equals total Joule heating P = ε² / R_tot = 0.968 W.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Evaluates magnetic braking force BIL without multiplying by speed v.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Calculates only the power dissipated in the external load I²R, omitting heating I²r inside the rod.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Uses ε²/R and neglects the rod resistance r when finding loop current.

items.stem: Travelling to the left at constant velocity 8 m s⁻¹, a crossbar of resistance 1 Ω spans frictionless rails 0.2 m apart on a frictionless laboratory induction sled connected to a 1.4 Ω load in a 0.35 T field (directed out of the page). What induced current circulates around the closed loop?
items.workedSolution: Motional emf ε = BLv = 0.35 × 0.2 × 8 = 0.560 V. Loop current I = ε / (R + r) = 0.560 / 2.4 = 0.233 A.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Divides by rail separation L instead of multiplying in ε = BLv.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Stops after computing motional emf ε = BLv without dividing by total resistance.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Divides motional emf BLv by external resistance R only, ignoring the rod resistance r.

items.stem: Within a drop-tower eddy-braking crossbar, a 2.4 Ω load terminates smooth rails separated by 0.32 m in a uniform 0.75 T field directed into the page, while a sliding rod (resistance 1.2 Ω) is driven to the right at 4 m s⁻¹. What external pulling force magnitude is needed to maintain this constant speed?
items.workedSolution: Motional emf ε = BLv = 0.960 V. Total loop resistance R_tot = 2.4 + 1.2 = 3.6 Ω, giving I = ε / R_tot = 0.267 A. Pulling force F = BIL = 0.0640 N.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates ε = BLv, I = ε/(R + r), and F = BIL = 0.0640 N (B).

options.distractorRationale: Stops after evaluating the induced loop current I = BLv/(R + r) without multiplying by B L.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Computes mechanical input power P = Fv instead of the applied pulling force F.

items.stem: During a steady-state run on a space-tether electrodynamic rail rig, a conducting rod of resistance 0.4 Ω glides right at 8 m s⁻¹ across rails 0.5 m apart bridged by 4.2 Ω in a 1.25 T magnetic field (directed out of the page). What is the terminal potential difference across the external load resistor?
items.workedSolution: ε = BLv = 5.00 V; loop current I = ε / (R + r) = 1.09 A. Terminal p.d. across load V_term = I R = 1.09 × 4.2 = 4.57 V.

markScheme.criterion: Uses V_term = BLv × R/(R + r) to obtain 4.57 V (B).

options.distractorRationale: Inverts the potential-divider ratio as ε(R + r)/R instead of εR/(R + r).

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Calculates the lost volts I r inside the moving rod instead of V_term = I R across the load.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Reports the full motional emf BLv and ignores the internal potential drop I r across the moving rod.

items.stem: On a levitated glider regenerator bench, a conducting bar of internal resistance 0.6 Ω slides to the left at a steady speed of 4 m s⁻¹ along parallel horizontal rails of negligible resistance spaced 0.2 m apart. A uniform 0.45 T magnetic field (directed into the page) threads the rails, which are bridged by a 1.4 Ω load resistor. What mechanical power must be supplied to keep the rod moving at constant speed?
items.workedSolution: ε = BLv = 0.360 V; R_tot = 1.4 + 0.6 = 2 Ω. Mechanical input power equals total Joule heating P = ε² / R_tot = 0.0648 W.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Evaluates magnetic braking force BIL without multiplying by speed v.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Uses ε²/R and neglects the rod resistance r when finding loop current.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Calculates only the power dissipated in the external load I²R, omitting heating I²r inside the rod.

items.stem: A uniform 0.9 T magnetic field directed out of the page permeates a electromagnetic rail-braking demonstrator whose smooth conducting rails sit 0.32 m apart across a 2.4 Ω external resistor. An external agent pulls a rod of resistance 0.8 Ω to the right at constant speed 8 m s⁻¹. What induced current circulates around the closed loop?
items.workedSolution: Motional emf ε = BLv = 0.9 × 0.32 × 8 = 2.30 V. Loop current I = ε / (R + r) = 2.30 / 3.2 = 0.720 A.

items.stem: In a linear regenerator test track, parallel rails of separation 0.5 m are closed by a 4.2 Ω resistor inside a perpendicular 0.25 T magnetic field (directed into the page). A metal rod of resistance 1 Ω moves steadily to the right at 4 m s⁻¹. What external pulling force magnitude is needed to maintain this constant speed?
items.workedSolution: Motional emf ε = BLv = 0.500 V. Total loop resistance R_tot = 4.2 + 1 = 5.2 Ω, giving I = ε / R_tot = 0.0962 A. Pulling force F = BIL = 0.0120 N.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates ε = BLv, I = ε/(R + r), and F = BIL = 0.0120 N (A).

options.distractorRationale: Computes mechanical input power P = Fv instead of the applied pulling force F.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Stops after evaluating the induced loop current I = BLv/(R + r) without multiplying by B L.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Neglects the internal resistance of the moving rod and divides by the external load resistance R alone.

items.stem: Travelling to the left at constant velocity 8 m s⁻¹, a crossbar of resistance 1.2 Ω spans frictionless rails 0.2 m apart on a magnetohydrodynamic copper-bar carriage connected to a 1.4 Ω load in a 0.6 T field (directed out of the page). What is the terminal potential difference across the external load resistor?
items.workedSolution: ε = BLv = 0.960 V; loop current I = ε / (R + r) = 0.369 A. Terminal p.d. across load V_term = I R = 0.369 × 1.4 = 0.517 V.

markScheme.criterion: Uses V_term = BLv × R/(R + r) to obtain 0.517 V (A).

options.distractorRationale: Calculates the lost volts I r inside the moving rod instead of V_term = I R across the load.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Inverts the potential-divider ratio as ε(R + r)/R instead of εR/(R + r).

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Reports the full motional emf BLv and ignores the internal potential drop I r across the moving rod.

items.stem: Within a frictionless laboratory induction sled, a 2.4 Ω load terminates smooth rails separated by 0.32 m in a uniform 1.1 T field directed into the page, while a sliding rod (resistance 0.4 Ω) is driven to the right at 4 m s⁻¹. What mechanical power must be supplied to keep the rod moving at constant speed?
items.workedSolution: ε = BLv = 1.41 V; R_tot = 2.4 + 0.4 = 2.8 Ω. Mechanical input power equals total Joule heating P = ε² / R_tot = 0.708 W.

items.stem: During a steady-state run on a drop-tower eddy-braking crossbar, a conducting rod of resistance 0.6 Ω glides right at 8 m s⁻¹ across rails 0.5 m apart bridged by 4.2 Ω in a 0.35 T magnetic field (directed out of the page). What induced current circulates around the closed loop?
items.workedSolution: Motional emf ε = BLv = 0.35 × 0.5 × 8 = 1.40 V. Loop current I = ε / (R + r) = 1.40 / 4.8 = 0.292 A.

items.stem: On a space-tether electrodynamic rail rig, a conducting bar of internal resistance 0.8 Ω slides to the left at a steady speed of 4 m s⁻¹ along parallel horizontal rails of negligible resistance spaced 0.2 m apart. A uniform 0.75 T magnetic field (directed into the page) threads the rails, which are bridged by a 1.4 Ω load resistor. What external pulling force magnitude is needed to maintain this constant speed?
items.workedSolution: Motional emf ε = BLv = 0.600 V. Total loop resistance R_tot = 1.4 + 0.8 = 2.2 Ω, giving I = ε / R_tot = 0.273 A. Pulling force F = BIL = 0.0409 N.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates ε = BLv, I = ε/(R + r), and F = BIL = 0.0409 N (B).

items.stem: In a hydroelectric micro-turbine alternator, a rectangular coil of 50 turns and cross-sectional area 0.01 m² rotates steadily at 20 Hz inside a uniform 0.14 T magnetic field, passing through maximum flux linkage at t = 0 and sampled at t = 0.00417 s. What is the peak emf ε₀ generated by the rotating coil?
items.workedSolution: Angular speed ω = 2πf = 2π(20) = 126 rad s⁻¹. Peak emf ε₀ = NBAω = 50 × 0.14 × 0.01 × 126 = 8.80 V.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Computes single-turn peak emf BAω and omits multiplying by N turns.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Doubles the amplitude and reports peak-to-peak emf 2ε₀ instead of peak emf ε₀.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Substitutes rotational frequency f directly into NBAω instead of angular speed ω = 2πf, omitting the 2π factor.

items.stem: An armature of 80 turns and area 0.018 m² in a wind-tunnel slip-ring test dynamo spins at frequency 40 Hz within a uniform 0.35 T field; its coil normal is aligned with the field at t = 0, and an oscilloscope reads the output at t = 0.00417 s. What instantaneous emf ε is induced at t = 0.00417 s?
items.workedSolution: ω = 2π(40) = 251 rad s⁻¹, ε₀ = NBAω = 127 V. At t = 0.00417 s, ε(t) = ε₀ sin(ωt) = 110 V.

markScheme.criterion: Computes ε₀ = 2πfNBA and evaluates ε₀ sin(ωt) = 110 V (C).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Omits 2π when computing peak amplitude NBAω before multiplying by sin(ωt).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Reports the maximum amplitude ε₀ rather than evaluating ε(t) = ε₀ sin(ωt) at the specified instant.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Evaluates ε₀ cos(ωt) instead of ε₀ sin(ωt), confusing the phase of induced emf with magnetic flux linkage.

items.stem: Driven at a rotational frequency of 60 Hz inside a bicycle hub-generator demonstrator, a slip-ring coil of 120 turns and area 0.03 m² cuts a uniform 0.14 T magnetic field (starting from maximum flux at t = 0 and observed at t = 0.00139 s). What is the peak-to-peak emf displayed on an oscilloscope across one full cycle?
items.workedSolution: Peak emf ε₀ = 2πfNBA = 190 V. Peak-to-peak emf V_pp = 2ε₀ = 380 V.

items.stem: Within a bicycle hub-generator demonstrator, uniform magnetic flux of density 0.35 T links a rotor coil of 80 turns and area 0.01 m² rotating at 60 Hz from maximum flux linkage at t = 0 up to t = 0.00278 s. What is the peak emf ε₀ generated by the rotating coil?
items.workedSolution: Angular speed ω = 2πf = 2π(60) = 377 rad s⁻¹. Peak emf ε₀ = NBAω = 80 × 0.35 × 0.01 × 377 = 106 V.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Doubles the amplitude and reports peak-to-peak emf 2ε₀ instead of peak emf ε₀.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Computes single-turn peak emf BAω and omits multiplying by N turns.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Substitutes rotational frequency f directly into NBAω instead of angular speed ω = 2πf, omitting the 2π factor.

items.stem: During testing of a portable Diesel-coupled AC armature, a coil with 120 turns and area 0.018 m² revolves at 100 Hz in a 0.14 T field, starting perpendicular to the field lines at t = 0 and queried at t = 8.33 × 10⁻⁴ s. What instantaneous emf ε is induced at t = 8.33 × 10⁻⁴ s?
items.workedSolution: ω = 2π(100) = 628 rad s⁻¹, ε₀ = NBAω = 190 V. At t = 8.33 × 10⁻⁴ s, ε(t) = ε₀ sin(ωt) = 95.0 V.

markScheme.criterion: Computes ε₀ = 2πfNBA and evaluates ε₀ sin(ωt) = 95.0 V (C).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Reports the maximum amplitude ε₀ rather than evaluating ε(t) = ε₀ sin(ωt) at the specified instant.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Evaluates ε₀ cos(ωt) instead of ε₀ sin(ωt), confusing the phase of induced emf with magnetic flux linkage.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Omits 2π when computing peak amplitude NBAω before multiplying by sin(ωt).

items.stem: Rotating uniformly at 25 Hz in a 0.35 T magnetic field, the coil (150 turns, area 0.03 m²) of a laboratory hand-cranked slip-ring coil starts at peak flux linkage at t = 0 and reaches t = 0.00667 s. What is the peak-to-peak emf displayed on an oscilloscope across one full cycle?
items.workedSolution: Peak emf ε₀ = 2πfNBA = 247 V. Peak-to-peak emf V_pp = 2ε₀ = 495 V.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Multiplies by 2 for peak-to-peak but omits 2π when converting f to ω.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Computes rms voltage ε₀/√2 instead of peak-to-peak voltage 2ε₀.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Reports single-sided peak amplitude ε₀ rather than peak-to-peak swing 2ε₀.

items.stem: In a tidal-stream rotor testbed, a rectangular coil of 200 turns and cross-sectional area 0.01 m² rotates steadily at 50 Hz inside a uniform 0.14 T magnetic field, passing through maximum flux linkage at t = 0 and sampled at t = 0.00167 s. What is the peak emf ε₀ generated by the rotating coil?
items.workedSolution: Angular speed ω = 2πf = 2π(50) = 314 rad s⁻¹. Peak emf ε₀ = NBAω = 200 × 0.14 × 0.01 × 314 = 88.0 V.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Computes single-turn peak emf BAω and omits multiplying by N turns.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Substitutes rotational frequency f directly into NBAω instead of angular speed ω = 2πf, omitting the 2π factor.

options.label: D

items.stem: In a laboratory slip-ring alternator with ohmic load, a winding of 280 turns and cross-sectional area 0.025 m² revolves at 50 Hz within a 0.16 T field and supplies sinusoidal AC directly to a 40 Ω resistive load. What mean electrical power is dissipated in the resistive load over a complete cycle?
items.workedSolution: Peak emf ε₀ = 2πfNBA = 352 V; V_rms = ε₀ / √2 = 249 V. Mean resistive power P_mean = V_rms² / R = ½ ε₀² / R = 1.55 × 10³ W.

markScheme.criterion: Computes ε₀ = 2πfNBA and mean power P_mean = ½ε₀²/R = 1.55 × 10³ W (A).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Divides peak power V₀I₀ by √2 instead of 2, forgetting that both V_rms = V₀/√2 and I_rms = I₀/√2 contribute a 1/√2 factor.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Calculates peak instantaneous power V₀²/R without applying the ½ sinusoidal average factor.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Divides V₀ by 2 instead of √2 before squaring in V_rms²/R, introducing a ¼ factor.

items.stem: Across a pure 25 Ω load in a wind-turbine test generator driving a load bank, a coil of 140 turns and area 0.025 m² (negligible coil resistance) rotates uniformly at 40 Hz inside a 0.38 T magnetic field. What is the root-mean-square (rms) potential difference across the load?
items.workedSolution: Peak emf ε₀ = 2πfNBA = 2π(40)(140)(0.38)(0.025) = 334 V. Therefore V_rms = ε₀ / √2 = 236 V.

markScheme.criterion: Finds ε₀ = 2πfNBA and divides by √2 to obtain 236 V (A).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Multiplies peak emf ε₀ by √2 instead of dividing by √2.

options.distractorRationale: Stops at peak emf ε₀ = 2πfNBA without dividing by √2.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Divides peak emf ε₀ by 2 (confusing the ½ power factor with the 1/√2 rms voltage factor).

items.stem: In a hospital X-ray filament supply transformer having primary winding N_p = 1200 and secondary winding N_s = 2400, a 200 V rms input drives a 6 Ω secondary load at overall power efficiency η = 0.92 (92%). What mean thermal power is wasted in the transformer core and windings?
items.workedSolution: V_s = 400 V; P_out = V_s² / R_L = 2.67 × 10⁴ W. Input power P_in = P_out / η = 2.90 × 10⁴ W, so power loss P_loss = P_in − P_out = 2.32 × 10³ W.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates P_in = P_out/η and P_loss = P_in − P_out = 2.32 × 10³ W (A).

items.stem: During thermal-loss testing of a arc-welding laminated-core transformer, a 230 V rms primary supply energises 300 primary turns coupled to 15 secondary turns across a 16 Ω load with efficiency η = 0.96 (96%). What rms current is drawn from the primary AC supply?
items.workedSolution: Secondary rms voltage V_s = V_p(N_s/N_p) = 230(15/300) = 11.5 V. Output power P_out = V_s² / R_L = 8.27 W. Input power P_in = P_out / η = 8.61 W, so I_p = P_in / V_p = 0.0374 A.

markScheme.criterion: Computes V_s, P_out, and I_p = P_out / (η V_p) = 0.0374 A (C).

items.stem: Across a 48 Ω secondary load, a railway signalling trackside transformer (500 primary turns, 100 secondary turns) transfers AC power from a 240 V rms source at efficiency 0.85 (85%). What is the rms potential difference induced across the secondary winding?
items.workedSolution: Using V_s / V_p = N_s / N_p gives V_s = 240 × (100 / 500) = 48.0 V.

items.stem: A laboratory bench variac step-down core with 1600 primary turns and 80 secondary turns operates at an efficiency of 0.95 (95%) from a 500 V rms AC supply while driving a 32 Ω resistive secondary load. What rms current is drawn from the primary AC supply?

markScheme.criterion: Computes V_s, P_out, and I_p = P_out / (η V_p) = 0.0411 A (C).

items.stem: In a rack-mounted server isolation-stepdown unit having primary winding N_p = 800 and secondary winding N_s = 1600, a 120 V rms input drives a 24 Ω secondary load at overall power efficiency η = 0.88 (88%). What mean thermal power is wasted in the transformer core and windings?
items.workedSolution: V_s = 240 V; P_out = V_s² / R_L = 2.40 × 10³ W. Input power P_in = P_out / η = 2.73 × 10³ W, so power loss P_loss = P_in − P_out = 327 W.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates P_in = P_out/η and P_loss = P_in − P_out = 327 W (D).

items.stem: During thermal-loss testing of a hospital X-ray filament supply transformer, a 200 V rms primary supply energises 1200 primary turns coupled to 60 secondary turns across a 6 Ω load with efficiency η = 0.92 (92%). What rms current is drawn from the primary AC supply?
items.workedSolution: Secondary rms voltage V_s = V_p(N_s/N_p) = 200(60/1200) = 10.0 V. Output power P_out = V_s² / R_L = 16.7 W. Input power P_in = P_out / η = 18.1 W, so I_p = P_in / V_p = 0.0906 A.

markScheme.criterion: Computes V_s, P_out, and I_p = P_out / (η V_p) = 0.0906 A (A).

items.stem: Across a 16 Ω secondary load, a arc-welding laminated-core transformer (300 primary turns, 60 secondary turns) transfers AC power from a 230 V rms source at efficiency 0.96 (96%). What is the rms potential difference induced across the secondary winding?
items.workedSolution: Using V_s / V_p = N_s / N_p gives V_s = 230 × (60 / 300) = 46.0 V.

items.stem: Operating at η = 0.85 (85%) efficiency from a 240 V rms AC source, a laminated-core railway signalling trackside transformer has N_p = 500 turns, N_s = 1000 turns, and a 48 Ω secondary load resistor. What mean thermal power is wasted in the transformer core and windings?
items.workedSolution: V_s = 480 V; P_out = V_s² / R_L = 4.80 × 10³ W. Input power P_in = P_out / η = 5.65 × 10³ W, so power loss P_loss = P_in − P_out = 847 W.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates P_in = P_out/η and P_loss = P_in − P_out = 847 W (D).

items.stem: A solar micro-inverter grid-coupling transformer with 1000 primary turns and 50 secondary turns operates at an efficiency of 0.9 (90%) from a 400 V rms AC supply while driving a 12 Ω resistive secondary load. What rms current is drawn from the primary AC supply?
items.workedSolution: Secondary rms voltage V_s = V_p(N_s/N_p) = 400(50/1000) = 20.0 V. Output power P_out = V_s² / R_L = 33.3 W. Input power P_in = P_out / η = 37.0 W, so I_p = P_in / V_p = 0.0926 A.

markScheme.criterion: Computes V_s, P_out, and I_p = P_out / (η V_p) = 0.0926 A (B).

items.stem: In a electrostatic cathode-ray oscilloscope tube, a electron (charge −1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C, mass 9.11 × 10⁻³¹ kg) enters horizontally at 1.40 × 10⁷ m s⁻¹ along the midplane between parallel deflecting plates of length 0.04 m and separation 0.05 m maintained at 959 V (neglecting gravity). What is the magnitude of the transverse deflection as the particle exits the plates?
items.workedSolution: Transit time t = L / v₀ = 0.04 / 1.40 × 10⁷ = 2.86 × 10⁻⁹ s. Transverse acceleration a_y = |q|V / (md) = 3.37 × 10¹⁵ m s⁻². Deflection |Δy| = ½ a_y t² = 0.0137 m.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates t = L/v₀, a_y = |q|V/(md), and |Δy| = ½a_y t² = 0.0137 m (C).

items.stem: Travelling at an initial horizontal speed of 5.00 × 10⁵ m s⁻¹, a proton (q = +1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C, m = 1.67 × 10⁻²⁷ kg) passes centrally between parallel plates of length 0.05 m spaced 0.04 m apart across a 1140 V potential difference in a inkjet micro-droplet deflection stage. What is the angular deflection θ (in degrees) of the particle velocity as it leaves the plates?
items.workedSolution: |v_y| = a_y t = (|q|V / md)(L / v₀) = 2.73 × 10⁵ m s⁻¹. Therefore θ = arctan(|v_y| / v₀) = 28.6°.

items.stem: Parallel plates of length 0.06 m and gap 0.06 m in a time-of-flight ion-beam steerer are held at 1170 V. A electron of charge −1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C and mass 9.11 × 10⁻³¹ kg enters midway between the plates parallel to their surfaces at 1.60 × 10⁷ m s⁻¹. What is the resultant speed of the particle as it emerges from the plates?
items.workedSolution: Exit transverse speed |v_y| = (|q|VL)/(md v₀) = 1.28 × 10⁷ m s⁻¹. Resultant speed v_exit = √(v₀² + v_y²) = 2.05 × 10⁷ m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates |v_y| and combines orthogonally v_exit = √(v₀² + v_y²) = 2.05 × 10⁷ m s⁻¹ (B).

items.stem: During calibration of a electron-beam lithography electrostatic deflector, a collimated proton beam (charge +1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C, mass 1.67 × 10⁻²⁷ kg) enters at 5.80 × 10⁵ m s⁻¹ along the central axis of 0.075 m long parallel electrodes separated by 0.05 m at p.d. 968 V. What is the magnitude of the transverse deflection as the particle exits the plates?
items.workedSolution: Transit time t = L / v₀ = 0.075 / 5.80 × 10⁵ = 1.29 × 10⁻⁷ s. Transverse acceleration a_y = |q|V / (md) = 1.85 × 10¹² m s⁻². Deflection |Δy| = ½ a_y t² = 0.0155 m.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates t = L/v₀, a_y = |q|V/(md), and |Δy| = ½a_y t² = 0.0155 m (C).

items.stem: Within an evacuated vacuum beam-diagnostics parallel-plate cell, a 341 V supply energises parallel plates of length 0.08 m and spacing 0.04 m while a electron (charge −1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C, mass 9.11 × 10⁻³¹ kg) enters horizontally at 1.80 × 10⁷ m s⁻¹. What is the angular deflection θ (in degrees) of the particle velocity as it leaves the plates?
items.workedSolution: |v_y| = a_y t = (|q|V / md)(L / v₀) = 6.65 × 10⁶ m s⁻¹. Therefore θ = arctan(|v_y| / v₀) = 20.3°.

items.stem: A proton with charge +1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C and mass 1.67 × 10⁻²⁷ kg is injected horizontally at 3.00 × 10⁵ m s⁻¹ into the uniform field of a electrostatic particle-beam chopper having plate length 0.09 m, plate separation 0.06 m, and applied voltage 230 V. What is the resultant speed of the particle as it emerges from the plates?
items.workedSolution: Exit transverse speed |v_y| = (|q|VL)/(md v₀) = 1.10 × 10⁵ m s⁻¹. Resultant speed v_exit = √(v₀² + v_y²) = 3.20 × 10⁵ m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates |v_y| and combines orthogonally v_exit = √(v₀² + v_y²) = 3.20 × 10⁵ m s⁻¹ (B).

items.stem: Across a 0.05 m vacuum gap of length 0.04 m inside a mass-spectrometer pre-filter electrostatic prism, a steady voltage of 2420 V deflects a horizontally incident electron (charge −1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C, mass 9.11 × 10⁻³¹ kg, entry speed 2.00 × 10⁷ m s⁻¹). What is the magnitude of the transverse deflection as the particle exits the plates?
items.workedSolution: Transit time t = L / v₀ = 0.04 / 2.00 × 10⁷ = 2.00 × 10⁻⁹ s. Transverse acceleration a_y = |q|V / (md) = 8.50 × 10¹⁵ m s⁻². Deflection |Δy| = ½ a_y t² = 0.0170 m.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates t = L/v₀, a_y = |q|V/(md), and |Δy| = ½a_y t² = 0.0170 m (B).

items.stem: Two flat conducting electrodes in a nanofabrication focused-beam blanking stage measure 0.06 m in length, sit 0.06 m apart, and carry 1710 V between them as a electron (−1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C, 9.11 × 10⁻³¹ kg) enters parallel to the plates at 2.20 × 10⁷ m s⁻¹. What is the resultant speed of the particle as it emerges from the plates?
items.workedSolution: Exit transverse speed |v_y| = (|q|VL)/(md v₀) = 1.37 × 10⁷ m s⁻¹. Resultant speed v_exit = √(v₀² + v_y²) = 2.59 × 10⁷ m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates |v_y| and combines orthogonally v_exit = √(v₀² + v_y²) = 2.59 × 10⁷ m s⁻¹ (D).

items.stem: Entering along the symmetry plane at 4.20 × 10⁵ m s⁻¹, a proton of charge +1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C and mass 1.67 × 10⁻²⁷ kg traverses a uniform transverse electric field created by 606 V across 0.075 m plates separated by 0.05 m in a synchrotron injector electrostatic kicker. What is the magnitude of the transverse deflection as the particle exits the plates?
items.workedSolution: Transit time t = L / v₀ = 0.075 / 4.20 × 10⁵ = 1.79 × 10⁻⁷ s. Transverse acceleration a_y = |q|V / (md) = 1.16 × 10¹² m s⁻². Deflection |Δy| = ½ a_y t² = 0.0185 m.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates t = L/v₀, a_y = |q|V/(md), and |Δy| = ½a_y t² = 0.0185 m (C).

items.stem: An engineer operates a photoelectron spectrometer deflection channel with 153 V applied across parallel steering plates of length 0.08 m and separation 0.04 m; each electron (−1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C, 9.11 × 10⁻³¹ kg) enters horizontally at 1.40 × 10⁷ m s⁻¹. What is the angular deflection θ (in degrees) of the particle velocity as it leaves the plates?
items.workedSolution: |v_y| = a_y t = (|q|V / md)(L / v₀) = 3.84 × 10⁶ m s⁻¹. Therefore θ = arctan(|v_y| / v₀) = 15.3°.

items.stem: Inside the vacuum chamber of a inkjet micro-droplet deflection stage, electrodes 0.04 m long and 0.05 m apart are biased at 1820 V while a electron (q = −1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C, m = 9.11 × 10⁻³¹ kg) enters centrally at 1.60 × 10⁷ m s⁻¹. What is the magnitude of the transverse deflection as the particle exits the plates?
items.workedSolution: Transit time t = L / v₀ = 0.04 / 1.60 × 10⁷ = 2.50 × 10⁻⁹ s. Transverse acceleration a_y = |q|V / (md) = 6.39 × 10¹⁵ m s⁻². Deflection |Δy| = ½ a_y t² = 0.0200 m.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates t = L/v₀, a_y = |q|V/(md), and |Δy| = ½a_y t² = 0.0200 m (B).

items.stem: Inside a fine-beam Helmholtz tube, a electron (charge −1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C, mass 9.11 × 10⁻³¹ kg) enters at 8.00 × 10⁶ m s⁻¹ perpendicular to a uniform 2.40 × 10⁻³ T magnetic field directed into the page and follows a circular arc. What is the radius of curvature r of the circular path?
items.workedSolution: Equating magnetic and centripetal forces |q|vB = mv²/r gives r = mv / (|q|B) = (9.11 × 10⁻³¹ kg × 8.00 × 10⁶) / (0 × 2.40 × 10⁻³) = 0.0190 m.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Inverts the cyclotron radius formula and evaluates |q|B / (mv) instead of mv / (|q|B).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Confuses orbital radius r = mv/(|q|B) with semicircular orbit diameter D = 2r.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Uses mv²/(|q|B) by forgetting to cancel one power of speed v when equating mv²/r = |q|vB.

items.stem: A uniform 0.480 T magnetic field (directed out of the page) fills a medical radioisotope cyclotron chamber. Entering at right angles to the field with speed 4.50 × 10⁶ m s⁻¹, a single proton of charge +1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C and mass 1.67 × 10⁻²⁷ kg curves along a circular trajectory. If the particle completes a semicircular turn to strike a flat detector wall on the entry plane, how far from the entry slit does it hit?
items.workedSolution: Cyclotron radius r = mv / (|q|B) = 0.0979 m. Across a semicircular turn, the impact distance from the entry slit equals the orbit diameter D = 2r = 0.196 m.

markScheme.criterion: Finds r = mv/(|q|B) and doubles to diameter D = 2r = 0.196 m (B).

items.stem: Injected orthogonally at 2.20 × 10⁶ m s⁻¹ into the 0.220 T magnetic field (directed into the page) of a bubble-chamber momentum analyser, a alpha particle (q = +3.20 × 10⁻¹⁹ C, m = 6.64 × 10⁻²⁷ kg) undergoes uniform circular motion in vacuum. What is the cyclotron revolution frequency f of the particle in this magnetic field?

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Inverts the formula and evaluates orbital period 2πm / (|q|B) instead of frequency.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Computes angular speed ω = |q|B / m and omits dividing by 2π for frequency f = ω / (2π).

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Divides ω by π instead of 2π when converting angular speed to frequency.

items.stem: During a beam run in a synchrotron dipole bending sector, a electron carrying charge −1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C and mass 9.11 × 10⁻³¹ kg moves at 2.60 × 10⁷ m s⁻¹ normal to a 3.50 × 10⁻³ T field directed out of the page. What is the radius of curvature r of the circular path?
items.workedSolution: Equating magnetic and centripetal forces |q|vB = mv²/r gives r = mv / (|q|B) = (9.11 × 10⁻³¹ kg × 2.60 × 10⁷) / (0 × 3.50 × 10⁻³) = 0.0423 m.

items.stem: Within the evacuated auroral plasma simulation chamber, a perpendicular magnetic field of flux density 0.640 T (directed into the page) bends a proton (charge +1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C, mass 1.67 × 10⁻²⁷ kg) travelling at 3.40 × 10⁶ m s⁻¹. If the particle completes a semicircular turn to strike a flat detector wall on the entry plane, how far from the entry slit does it hit?
items.workedSolution: Cyclotron radius r = mv / (|q|B) = 0.0554 m. Across a semicircular turn, the impact distance from the entry slit equals the orbit diameter D = 2r = 0.111 m.

markScheme.criterion: Finds r = mv/(|q|B) and doubles to diameter D = 2r = 0.111 m (D).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Inverts the formula and evaluates orbital period 2πm / (|q|B) instead of frequency.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Divides ω by π instead of 2π when converting angular speed to frequency.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Computes angular speed ω = |q|B / m and omits dividing by 2π for frequency f = ω / (2π).

items.stem: Magnetic flux of density 4.80 × 10⁻³ T (directed into the page) pervades the vacuum region of a proton-therapy gantry bending magnet where a electron of mass 9.11 × 10⁻³¹ kg and charge −1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C circulates at constant speed 2.10 × 10⁷ m s⁻¹ normal to the field lines. What is the radius of curvature r of the circular path?
items.workedSolution: Equating magnetic and centripetal forces |q|vB = mv²/r gives r = mv / (|q|B) = (9.11 × 10⁻³¹ kg × 2.10 × 10⁷) / (0 × 4.80 × 10⁻³) = 0.0249 m.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Confuses orbital radius r = mv/(|q|B) with semicircular orbit diameter D = 2r.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Inverts the cyclotron radius formula and evaluates |q|B / (mv) instead of mv / (|q|B).

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Uses mv²/(|q|B) by forgetting to cancel one power of speed v when equating mv²/r = |q|vB.

items.stem: An experimenter fires a proton (+1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C, 1.67 × 10⁻²⁷ kg) at speed 2.60 × 10⁶ m s⁻¹ at 90° to a uniform 0.160 T field directed out of the page inside a storage-ring magnetic spectrometer arc. If the particle completes a semicircular turn to strike a flat detector wall on the entry plane, how far from the entry slit does it hit?
items.workedSolution: Cyclotron radius r = mv / (|q|B) = 0.170 m. Across a semicircular turn, the impact distance from the entry slit equals the orbit diameter D = 2r = 0.339 m.

markScheme.criterion: Finds r = mv/(|q|B) and doubles to diameter D = 2r = 0.339 m (B).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Reports the cyclotron radius r instead of the semicircular chord diameter D = 2r along the detector wall.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Doubles the diameter a second time and reports 4r instead of 2r.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Calculates the curved semicircular arc length πr rather than the straight-line wall separation 2r.

items.stem: Subject solely to the magnetic Lorentz force in a space-radiation geomagnetic trap simulator, a alpha particle (mass 6.64 × 10⁻²⁷ kg, charge +3.20 × 10⁻¹⁹ C) enters at 5.20 × 10⁶ m s⁻¹ orthogonal to a steady 0.450 T field directed into the page. What is the cyclotron revolution frequency f of the particle in this magnetic field?

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Inverts the formula and evaluates orbital period 2πm / (|q|B) instead of frequency.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Computes angular speed ω = |q|B / m and omits dividing by 2π for frequency f = ω / (2π).

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Divides ω by π instead of 2π when converting angular speed to frequency.

items.stem: Crossing the entry slit of a high-vacuum Lorentz curvature cell at 1.50 × 10⁷ m s⁻¹, a electron with charge −1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C and mass 9.11 × 10⁻³¹ kg encounters a uniform perpendicular 6.40 × 10⁻³ T magnetic field (directed out of the page). What is the radius of curvature r of the circular path?
items.workedSolution: Equating magnetic and centripetal forces |q|vB = mv²/r gives r = mv / (|q|B) = (9.11 × 10⁻³¹ kg × 1.50 × 10⁷) / (0 × 6.40 × 10⁻³) = 0.0133 m.

items.stem: In high vacuum within a positron-emission cyclotron target injector, coils maintain a uniform 0.250 T field directed into the page at right angles to an incident proton (+1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C, 1.67 × 10⁻²⁷ kg) travelling at 1.80 × 10⁶ m s⁻¹. If the particle completes a semicircular turn to strike a flat detector wall on the entry plane, how far from the entry slit does it hit?
items.workedSolution: Cyclotron radius r = mv / (|q|B) = 0.0752 m. Across a semicircular turn, the impact distance from the entry slit equals the orbit diameter D = 2r = 0.150 m.

markScheme.criterion: Finds r = mv/(|q|B) and doubles to diameter D = 2r = 0.150 m (B).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Reports the cyclotron radius r instead of the semicircular chord diameter D = 2r along the detector wall.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Calculates the curved semicircular arc length πr rather than the straight-line wall separation 2r.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Doubles the diameter a second time and reports 4r instead of 2r.

items.stem: Travelling through a fine-beam Helmholtz tube with speed 4.20 × 10⁶ m s⁻¹ normal to magnetic field lines of strength 0.600 T (directed out of the page), a alpha particle of charge +3.20 × 10⁻¹⁹ C and mass 6.64 × 10⁻²⁷ kg executes circular motion. What is the cyclotron revolution frequency f of the particle in this magnetic field?

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Divides ω by π instead of 2π when converting angular speed to frequency.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Inverts the formula and evaluates orbital period 2πm / (|q|B) instead of frequency.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Computes angular speed ω = |q|B / m and omits dividing by 2π for frequency f = ω / (2π).

items.stem: A collimated electron (q = −1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C, m = 9.11 × 10⁻³¹ kg) enters a medical radioisotope cyclotron chamber at 1.20 × 10⁷ m s⁻¹ perpendicular to a homogeneous 1.50 × 10⁻³ T magnetic field directed into the page. What is the radius of curvature r of the circular path?
items.workedSolution: Equating magnetic and centripetal forces |q|vB = mv²/r gives r = mv / (|q|B) = (9.11 × 10⁻³¹ kg × 1.20 × 10⁷) / (0 × 1.50 × 10⁻³) = 0.0456 m.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Confuses orbital radius r = mv/(|q|B) with semicircular orbit diameter D = 2r.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Inverts the cyclotron radius formula and evaluates |q|B / (mv) instead of mv / (|q|B).

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Uses mv²/(|q|B) by forgetting to cancel one power of speed v when equating mv²/r = |q|vB.

items.stem: In a semiconductor ion-implantation beamline, a electron (charge −1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C, mass 9.11 × 10⁻³¹ kg) starts from rest, accelerates across a potential difference of 250 V, and enters perpendicular to a uniform 2.50 × 10⁻³ T magnetic field (out of the page). What is the radius of the resulting circular path inside the magnetic field?
items.workedSolution: From ½mv² = |q|V_acc, speed v = √(2|q|V_acc / m) = 9.37 × 10⁶ m s⁻¹. Orbit radius r = mv / (|q|B) = (1/B)√(2mV_acc / |q|) = 0.0213 m.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Omits the factor of 2 inside v = √(2|q|V_acc/m) from forgetting ½ in ½mv² = |q|V_acc.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Confuses orbital radius r with semicircular diameter 2r.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Evaluates r² = 2mV_acc/(|q|B²) without taking the square root.

items.stem: Accelerated from rest through 2400 V in a Thomson e/m specific-charge apparatus, a singly ionised lithium ion of charge +1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C and mass 1.16 × 10⁻²⁶ kg passes into a uniform 0.450 T magnetic field directed into the page at right angles to its velocity. What speed does the particle reach upon entering the magnetic field?
items.workedSolution: Equating ½mv² = |q|V_acc gives v = √(2|q|V_acc / m) = √(2 × 0 × 2400 / 1.16 × 10⁻²⁶ kg) = 2.57 × 10⁵ m s⁻¹.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Forgets the ½ in ½mv² = |q|V_acc and computes √(|q|V_acc / m).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Multiplies by 4 instead of 2 inside the square root.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Computes v² = 2|q|V_acc / m without taking the square root.

items.stem: An electrostatic gun in a focused gallium-ion lithographic column accelerates a stationary doubly ionised magnesium ion (q = +3.20 × 10⁻¹⁹ C, m = 3.98 × 10⁻²⁶ kg) across 1500 V before injecting it orthogonally into a 0.320 T magnetic field (out of the page). If the particle completes a semicircular turn onto an exit detector plate, what is the strike diameter D from the entry slit?
items.workedSolution: Speed v = √(2|q|V_acc / m) = 1.55 × 10⁵ m s⁻¹; radius r = mv / (|q|B) = 0.0604 m. Semicircular detector separation D = 2r = 0.121 m.

options.distractorRationale: Omits the factor of 2 in v = √(2|q|V_acc/m) when computing r before doubling.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Reports the orbital radius r = (1/B)√(2mV_acc/|q|) instead of the semicircular chord diameter D = 2r.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Computes curved semicircular arc length πr rather than straight-line detector chord 2r.

items.stem: Within a secondary-ion mass analyser magnet, a electron carrying charge −1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C and mass 9.11 × 10⁻³¹ kg gains kinetic energy across an accelerating voltage of 1200 V from rest and then curves in a uniform 5.00 × 10⁻³ T magnetic field (into the page). What is the radius of the resulting circular path inside the magnetic field?
items.workedSolution: From ½mv² = |q|V_acc, speed v = √(2|q|V_acc / m) = 2.05 × 10⁷ m s⁻¹. Orbit radius r = mv / (|q|B) = (1/B)√(2mV_acc / |q|) = 0.0234 m.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Omits the factor of 2 inside v = √(2|q|V_acc/m) from forgetting ½ in ½mv² = |q|V_acc.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Confuses orbital radius r with semicircular diameter 2r.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Evaluates r² = 2mV_acc/(|q|B²) without taking the square root.

items.stem: During calibration of a electrostatic-gun magnetic spectrometer, initially stationary singly ionised lithium ions (charge +1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C, mass 1.16 × 10⁻²⁶ kg) are accelerated by 1800 V and directed normal to a 0.250 T field (out of the page). What speed does the particle reach upon entering the magnetic field?
items.workedSolution: Equating ½mv² = |q|V_acc gives v = √(2|q|V_acc / m) = √(2 × 0 × 1800 / 1.16 × 10⁻²⁶ kg) = 2.23 × 10⁵ m s⁻¹.

items.stem: Starting at negligible speed in a isotopic beam-separator bending magnet, a doubly ionised magnesium ion (charge +3.20 × 10⁻¹⁹ C, mass 3.98 × 10⁻²⁶ kg) traverses a 1000 V accelerating gap and enters a perpendicular 0.550 T magnetic field (into the page). If the particle completes a semicircular turn onto an exit detector plate, what is the strike diameter D from the entry slit?
items.workedSolution: Speed v = √(2|q|V_acc / m) = 1.27 × 10⁵ m s⁻¹; radius r = mv / (|q|B) = 0.0287 m. Semicircular detector separation D = 2r = 0.0574 m.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Omits the factor of 2 in v = √(2|q|V_acc/m) when computing r before doubling.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Computes curved semicircular arc length πr rather than straight-line detector chord 2r.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Reports the orbital radius r = (1/B)√(2mV_acc/|q|) instead of the semicircular chord diameter D = 2r.

items.stem: Released with zero initial kinetic energy inside a accelerator-mass-spectrometry injection sector, a electron (−1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C, 9.11 × 10⁻³¹ kg) falls through a potential difference of 900 V and immediately enters a uniform 2.50 × 10⁻³ T field out of the page normal to its path. What is the radius of the resulting circular path inside the magnetic field?
items.workedSolution: From ½mv² = |q|V_acc, speed v = √(2|q|V_acc / m) = 1.78 × 10⁷ m s⁻¹. Orbit radius r = mv / (|q|B) = (1/B)√(2mV_acc / |q|) = 0.0405 m.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Computes curved semicircular arc length πr rather than straight-line detector chord 2r.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Omits the factor of 2 in v = √(2|q|V_acc/m) when computing r before doubling.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Reports the orbital radius r = (1/B)√(2mV_acc/|q|) instead of the semicircular chord diameter D = 2r.

items.stem: Inside an evacuated vacuum cathode-ray magnetic deflection tube, a electron with mass 9.11 × 10⁻³¹ kg and charge −1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C is accelerated from rest by 600 V and bent along an arc by a perpendicular 5.00 × 10⁻³ T magnetic field (into the page). What is the radius of the resulting circular path inside the magnetic field?
items.workedSolution: From ½mv² = |q|V_acc, speed v = √(2|q|V_acc / m) = 1.45 × 10⁷ m s⁻¹. Orbit radius r = mv / (|q|B) = (1/B)√(2mV_acc / |q|) = 0.0165 m.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Omits the factor of 2 inside v = √(2|q|V_acc/m) from forgetting ½ in ½mv² = |q|V_acc.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Confuses orbital radius r with semicircular diameter 2r.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Evaluates r² = 2mV_acc/(|q|B²) without taking the square root.

items.stem: Before entering the uniform 0.250 T magnetic field (out of the page) of a nuclear astrophysics recoil separator at right angles, a singly ionised lithium ion (q = +1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C, m = 1.16 × 10⁻²⁶ kg) is accelerated from rest through an electrode voltage of 800 V. What speed does the particle reach upon entering the magnetic field?
items.workedSolution: Equating ½mv² = |q|V_acc gives v = √(2|q|V_acc / m) = √(2 × 0 × 800 / 1.16 × 10⁻²⁶ kg) = 1.49 × 10⁵ m s⁻¹.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Forgets the ½ in ½mv² = |q|V_acc and computes √(|q|V_acc / m).

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Computes v² = 2|q|V_acc / m without taking the square root.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Multiplies by 4 instead of 2 inside the square root.

items.stem: An extraction stage biased at 3000 V accelerates stationary doubly ionised magnesium ions (mass 3.98 × 10⁻²⁶ kg, charge +3.20 × 10⁻¹⁹ C) in a semiconductor ion-implantation beamline straight into a transverse 0.550 T magnetic field (into the page). If the particle completes a semicircular turn onto an exit detector plate, what is the strike diameter D from the entry slit?
items.workedSolution: Speed v = √(2|q|V_acc / m) = 2.20 × 10⁵ m s⁻¹; radius r = mv / (|q|B) = 0.0497 m. Semicircular detector separation D = 2r = 0.0993 m.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Computes curved semicircular arc length πr rather than straight-line detector chord 2r.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Reports the orbital radius r = (1/B)√(2mV_acc/|q|) instead of the semicircular chord diameter D = 2r.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Omits the factor of 2 in v = √(2|q|V_acc/m) when computing r before doubling.

items.stem: From rest at the ion source of a Thomson e/m specific-charge apparatus, a electron (−1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C, 9.11 × 10⁻³¹ kg) crosses a 400 V accelerating potential and enters normal to a steady 2.50 × 10⁻³ T magnetic field (out of the page). What is the radius of the resulting circular path inside the magnetic field?
items.workedSolution: From ½mv² = |q|V_acc, speed v = √(2|q|V_acc / m) = 1.19 × 10⁷ m s⁻¹. Orbit radius r = mv / (|q|B) = (1/B)√(2mV_acc / |q|) = 0.0270 m.

items.stem: In a Wien crossed-field velocity filter, parallel plates separated by 0.02 m are held at 180 V (upper plate positive) perpendicular to a uniform 0.12 T magnetic field (into the page). A proton (charge +1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C, mass 1.67 × 10⁻²⁷ kg) is injected horizontally along the central axis. At what speed must the proton travel to pass straight through the exit slit undeflected?
items.workedSolution: Uniform electric field E = V / d = 180 / 0.02 = 9.00 × 10³ V m⁻¹. Zero net deflection requires qE = qvB, so v_sel = E / B = V / (Bd) = 7.50 × 10⁴ m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Uses v_sel = V / (Bd) to obtain 7.50 × 10⁴ m s⁻¹ (A).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Multiplies E by B instead of dividing E / B in the balanced-force condition qE = qvB.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Multiplies V by d instead of dividing V by d when finding electric field E = V/d.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Inverts v = E/B and computes B/E = Bd/V instead of V/(Bd).

items.stem: A accelerator monochromatic ion collimator combines parallel electrodes 0.04 m apart at 320 V (upper plate negative) with a crossed 0.2 T magnetic field (out of the page) for protons (q = +1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C, m = 1.67 × 10⁻²⁷ kg) injected horizontally to the right at 2.40 × 10⁴ m s⁻¹. What is the initial upward transverse acceleration of the proton upon entering the crossed fields?
items.workedSolution: E = V/d = 8.00 × 10³ V m⁻¹. Upward electric force F_E = qE = 1.28 × 10⁻¹⁵ N; downward magnetic force |F_B| = qvB = 7.68 × 10⁻¹⁶ N. Net upward acceleration a_y = (F_E − |F_B|) / m = 3.07 × 10¹¹ m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts opposing qvB from qE and divides by m to obtain 3.07 × 10¹¹ m s⁻² (D).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Calculates only the magnetic acceleration magnitude qvB/m and ignores the electric field.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Adds the electric and magnetic force magnitudes (|F_E| + |F_B|)/m instead of subtracting opposing forces.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Includes only the upward electric acceleration qE/m and ignores the opposing downward magnetic force.

items.stem: Crossed fields in a accelerator-mass-spectrometry pre-filter are produced by 600 V across plates spaced 0.025 m apart (upper plate positive) and a 0.32 T field directed into the page; a proton (+1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C, 1.67 × 10⁻²⁷ kg) is injected horizontally along the central axis. At what speed must the proton travel to pass straight through the exit slit undeflected?
items.workedSolution: Uniform electric field E = V / d = 600 / 0.025 = 2.40 × 10⁴ V m⁻¹. Zero net deflection requires qE = qvB, so v_sel = E / B = V / (Bd) = 7.50 × 10⁴ m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Uses v_sel = V / (Bd) to obtain 7.50 × 10⁴ m s⁻¹ (B).

items.stem: Within a vacuum electron-microscope Wien monochromator, a proton (+1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C, 1.67 × 10⁻²⁷ kg) is injected horizontally to the right at 3.00 × 10⁵ m s⁻¹ between plates 0.015 m apart at p.d. 900 V (upper plate negative) inside a perpendicular 0.12 T field (out of the page). At what speed would a proton instead have to enter this same selector to pass straight through undeflected?
items.workedSolution: Electric field E = V / d = 900 / 0.015 = 6.00 × 10⁴ V m⁻¹. Undeflected transmission requires qvB = qE, giving v_sel = E / B = 5.00 × 10⁵ m s⁻¹.

items.stem: During tuning of a plasma neutral-beam ion velocity selector (240 V across a 0.03 m gap, upper plate positive, with B = 0.2 T into the page), a proton of charge +1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C and mass 1.67 × 10⁻²⁷ kg is injected horizontally along the central axis. At what speed must the proton travel to pass straight through the exit slit undeflected?
items.workedSolution: Uniform electric field E = V / d = 240 / 0.03 = 8.00 × 10³ V m⁻¹. Zero net deflection requires qE = qvB, so v_sel = E / B = V / (Bd) = 4.00 × 10⁴ m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Uses v_sel = V / (Bd) to obtain 4.00 × 10⁴ m s⁻¹ (D).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Multiplies E by B instead of dividing E / B in the balanced-force condition qE = qvB.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Inverts v = E/B and computes B/E = Bd/V instead of V/(Bd).

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Multiplies V by d instead of dividing V by d when finding electric field E = V/d.

items.stem: In a atomic-physics crossed-E/B beam gate, parallel plates separated by 0.02 m are held at 450 V (upper plate negative) perpendicular to a uniform 0.32 T magnetic field (out of the page). A proton (charge +1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C, mass 1.67 × 10⁻²⁷ kg) is injected horizontally to the right at 4.22 × 10⁴ m s⁻¹. What is the initial upward transverse acceleration of the proton upon entering the crossed fields?
items.workedSolution: E = V/d = 2.25 × 10⁴ V m⁻¹. Upward electric force F_E = qE = 3.60 × 10⁻¹⁵ N; downward magnetic force |F_B| = qvB = 2.16 × 10⁻¹⁵ N. Net upward acceleration a_y = (F_E − |F_B|) / m = 8.62 × 10¹¹ m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts opposing qvB from qE and divides by m to obtain 8.62 × 10¹¹ m s⁻² (C).

items.stem: A Wien crossed-field velocity filter combines parallel electrodes 0.04 m apart at 750 V (upper plate positive) with a crossed 0.12 T magnetic field (into the page) for protons (q = +1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C, m = 1.67 × 10⁻²⁷ kg) injected horizontally along the central axis. At what speed must the proton travel to pass straight through the exit slit undeflected?
items.workedSolution: Uniform electric field E = V / d = 750 / 0.04 = 1.88 × 10⁴ V m⁻¹. Zero net deflection requires qE = qvB, so v_sel = E / B = V / (Bd) = 1.56 × 10⁵ m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Uses v_sel = V / (Bd) to obtain 1.56 × 10⁵ m s⁻¹ (C).

items.stem: Crossed fields in a accelerator monochromatic ion collimator are produced by 180 V across plates spaced 0.025 m apart (upper plate negative) and a 0.2 T field directed out of the page; a proton (+1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C, 1.67 × 10⁻²⁷ kg) is injected horizontally to the right at 2.16 × 10⁴ m s⁻¹. At what speed would a proton instead have to enter this same selector to pass straight through undeflected?
items.workedSolution: Electric field E = V / d = 180 / 0.025 = 7.20 × 10³ V m⁻¹. Undeflected transmission requires qvB = qE, giving v_sel = E / B = 3.60 × 10⁴ m s⁻¹.

items.stem: Within a vacuum accelerator-mass-spectrometry pre-filter, a proton (+1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C, 1.67 × 10⁻²⁷ kg) is injected horizontally along the central axis between plates 0.015 m apart at p.d. 320 V (upper plate positive) inside a perpendicular 0.32 T field (into the page). At what speed must the proton travel to pass straight through the exit slit undeflected?
items.workedSolution: Uniform electric field E = V / d = 320 / 0.015 = 2.13 × 10⁴ V m⁻¹. Zero net deflection requires qE = qvB, so v_sel = E / B = V / (Bd) = 6.67 × 10⁴ m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Uses v_sel = V / (Bd) to obtain 6.67 × 10⁴ m s⁻¹ (A).
