options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Multiplies E by B instead of dividing E / B in the balanced-force condition qE = qvB.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Inverts v = E/B and computes B/E = Bd/V instead of V/(Bd).

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Multiplies V by d instead of dividing V by d when finding electric field E = V/d.

items.stem: During tuning of a electron-microscope Wien monochromator (600 V across a 0.03 m gap, upper plate negative, with B = 0.12 T out of the page), a proton of charge +1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C and mass 1.67 × 10⁻²⁷ kg is injected horizontally to the right at 1.00 × 10⁵ m s⁻¹. What is the initial upward transverse acceleration of the proton upon entering the crossed fields?
items.workedSolution: E = V/d = 2.00 × 10⁴ V m⁻¹. Upward electric force F_E = qE = 3.20 × 10⁻¹⁵ N; downward magnetic force |F_B| = qvB = 1.92 × 10⁻¹⁵ N. Net upward acceleration a_y = (F_E − |F_B|) / m = 7.66 × 10¹¹ m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts opposing qvB from qE and divides by m to obtain 7.66 × 10¹¹ m s⁻² (C).

options.distractorRationale: Includes only the upward electric acceleration qE/m and ignores the opposing downward magnetic force.

options.label: B

options.distractorRationale: Adds the electric and magnetic force magnitudes (|F_E| + |F_B|)/m instead of subtracting opposing forces.

items.stem: In a plasma neutral-beam ion velocity selector, parallel plates separated by 0.02 m are held at 900 V (upper plate positive) perpendicular to a uniform 0.2 T magnetic field (into the page). A proton (charge +1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C, mass 1.67 × 10⁻²⁷ kg) is injected horizontally along the central axis. At what speed must the proton travel to pass straight through the exit slit undeflected?
items.workedSolution: Uniform electric field E = V / d = 900 / 0.02 = 4.50 × 10⁴ V m⁻¹. Zero net deflection requires qE = qvB, so v_sel = E / B = V / (Bd) = 2.25 × 10⁵ m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Uses v_sel = V / (Bd) to obtain 2.25 × 10⁵ m s⁻¹ (B).

options.distractorRationale: Multiplies E by B instead of dividing E / B in the balanced-force condition qE = qvB.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Inverts v = E/B and computes B/E = Bd/V instead of V/(Bd).

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Multiplies V by d instead of dividing V by d when finding electric field E = V/d.

items.stem: A atomic-physics crossed-E/B beam gate combines parallel electrodes 0.04 m apart at 240 V (upper plate negative) with a crossed 0.32 T magnetic field (out of the page) for protons (q = +1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C, m = 1.67 × 10⁻²⁷ kg) injected horizontally to the right at 1.13 × 10⁴ m s⁻¹. At what speed would a proton instead have to enter this same selector to pass straight through undeflected?
items.workedSolution: Electric field E = V / d = 240 / 0.04 = 6.00 × 10³ V m⁻¹. Undeflected transmission requires qvB = qE, giving v_sel = E / B = 1.88 × 10⁴ m s⁻¹.

items.stem: Crossed fields in a Wien crossed-field velocity filter are produced by 450 V across plates spaced 0.025 m apart (upper plate positive) and a 0.12 T field directed into the page; a proton (+1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C, 1.67 × 10⁻²⁷ kg) is injected horizontally along the central axis. At what speed must the proton travel to pass straight through the exit slit undeflected?
items.workedSolution: Uniform electric field E = V / d = 450 / 0.025 = 1.80 × 10⁴ V m⁻¹. Zero net deflection requires qE = qvB, so v_sel = E / B = V / (Bd) = 1.50 × 10⁵ m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Uses v_sel = V / (Bd) to obtain 1.50 × 10⁵ m s⁻¹ (D).

options.distractorRationale: Inverts v = E/B and computes B/E = Bd/V instead of V/(Bd).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Multiplies V by d instead of dividing V by d when finding electric field E = V/d.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Multiplies E by B instead of dividing E / B in the balanced-force condition qE = qvB.

items.stem: In a geochronology Bainbridge isotope spectrometer, two carbon isotopes of equal charge +1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C and masses m₁ = 1.99 × 10⁻²⁶ kg and m₂ = 2.32 × 10⁻²⁶ kg pass undeflected through a velocity selector (E = 4.00 × 10⁴ V m⁻¹, B₁ = 0.25 T) before entering a semicircular analyser chamber with uniform field B₂ = 0.6 T (into the page). What is the straight-line separation ΔD between the two isotope strike marks on the detector wall?
items.workedSolution: Selected speed v = E / B₁ = 1.60 × 10⁵ m s⁻¹. Semicircular strike separation ΔD = 2(r₂ − r₁) = 2(m₂ − m₁)E / (q B₁ B₂) = 0.0110 m.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Reports the semicircular strike distance 2r₁ of the lighter isotope rather than the separation between isotopes.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Uses B₁² in the denominator instead of the product B₁B₂ of selector and chamber fields.

parts.prompt: Calculate the motional emf induced across the sliding rod.
Determine the induced current circulating around the rails.
Calculate the external pulling force magnitude required to maintain constant speed.

items.stem: In a electromagnetic rail-braking demonstrator, parallel rails of separation 0.5 m are closed by a 4.2 Ω resistor inside a perpendicular 0.45 T magnetic field (directed into the page). A metal rod of resistance 1.2 Ω moves steadily to the right at 4 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Divides ε from (a) by total loop resistance R + r.
Equates applied force to magnetic braking force F = BIL.

parts.prompt: Calculate the motional emf induced across the sliding rod.
Determine the induced current circulating around the rails.
Calculate the external pulling force magnitude required to maintain constant speed.

items.stem: A uniform 0.35 T magnetic field directed out of the page permeates a space-tether electrodynamic rail rig whose smooth conducting rails sit 0.32 m apart across a 2.4 Ω external resistor. An external agent pulls a rod of resistance 1.2 Ω to the right at constant speed 8 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Divides ε from (a) by total loop resistance R + r.
Equates applied force to magnetic braking force F = BIL.

parts.prompt: Calculate the speed at which the particle enters the magnetic field.
Determine the radius r of the circular trajectory.
Calculate the semicircular strike diameter D = 2r across an exit detector plane.

items.stem: During calibration of a accelerator-mass-spectrometry injection sector, initially stationary doubly ionised magnesium ions (charge +3.20 × 10⁻¹⁹ C, mass 3.98 × 10⁻²⁶ kg) are accelerated by 1500 V and directed normal to a 0.550 T field (into the page).

markScheme.criterion: Uses ½mv² = |q|V_acc to solve for v.
Applies r = mv / (|q|B) using v from (a).
Multiplies orbital radius from (b) by two.

Determine the radius r of the circular trajectory.
Calculate the semicircular strike diameter D = 2r across an exit detector plane.

items.stem: Released with zero initial kinetic energy inside a surface-science low-energy ion scattering rig, a singly ionised lithium ion (+1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C, 1.16 × 10⁻²⁶ kg) falls through a potential difference of 1800 V and immediately enters a uniform 0.450 T field into the page normal to its path.

markScheme.criterion: Uses ½mv² = |q|V_acc to solve for v.
Applies r = mv / (|q|B) using v from (a).
Multiplies orbital radius from (b) by two.

items.stem: Within a vacuum accelerator monochromatic ion collimator, a proton (+1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C, 1.67 × 10⁻²⁷ kg) is injected horizontally to the right at 1.50 × 10⁵ m s⁻¹ between plates 0.015 m apart at p.d. 750 V (upper plate negative) inside a perpendicular 0.2 T field (out of the page).

markScheme.criterion: Equates qE = qvB to obtain v_sel = E / B.

parts.prompt: Calculate the electric field magnitude E between the parallel plates.
Calculate the speed v_sel required for the proton to pass straight through undeflected.

items.stem: In a electron-microscope Wien monochromator, parallel plates separated by 0.02 m are held at 320 V (upper plate negative) perpendicular to a uniform 0.12 T magnetic field (out of the page). A proton (charge +1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C, mass 1.67 × 10⁻²⁷ kg) is injected horizontally to the right at 8.00 × 10⁴ m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Equates qE = qvB to obtain v_sel = E / B.

Calculate the initial upward acceleration of the injected proton.

items.stem: A plasma neutral-beam ion velocity selector combines parallel electrodes 0.04 m apart at 600 V (upper plate positive) with a crossed 0.2 T magnetic field (into the page) for protons (q = +1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C, m = 1.67 × 10⁻²⁷ kg) injected horizontally along the central axis.

markScheme.criterion: Sets qvB = qE so v_sel = E / B.

parts.prompt: Calculate the electric field magnitude E between the parallel plates.
Calculate the speed v_sel required for the proton to pass straight through undeflected.

items.stem: Crossed fields in a atomic-physics crossed-E/B beam gate are produced by 900 V across plates spaced 0.025 m apart (upper plate negative) and a 0.32 T field directed out of the page; a proton (+1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C, 1.67 × 10⁻²⁷ kg) is injected horizontally to the right at 6.75 × 10⁴ m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Equates qE = qvB to obtain v_sel = E / B.

items.stem: A ceramic capacitive pressure transducer consists of parallel conducting plates of overlapping area 0.32 m² separated by a uniform alumina ceramic layer of thickness 2.50 × 10⁻⁴ m and relative permittivity 3.8. A steady potential difference of 150 V is maintained across the plates (ε₀ = 8.85 × 10⁻¹² F m⁻¹). What electrostatic energy is stored in the capacitor?

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates C = εᵣε₀A/d and U = ½CV² to obtain 4.84 × 10⁻⁴ J (B).

items.stem: A laboratory prototype of a high-voltage laser flashlamp cell employs parallel electrodes of area 1.1 m², a cast epoxy resin dielectric of thickness 5.00 × 10⁻⁴ m and relative permittivity 6.8, and a charging supply of 150 V (ε₀ = 8.85 × 10⁻¹² F m⁻¹). What magnitude of charge is stored on each conducting plate?
items.workedSolution: Capacitance C = εᵣε₀A / d = 1.32 × 10⁻⁷ F. Plate charge Q = CV = 1.32 × 10⁻⁷ × 150 = 1.99 × 10⁻⁵ C.

markScheme.criterion: Combines C = εᵣε₀A/d with Q = CV to obtain 1.99 × 10⁻⁵ C (B).

items.stem: During a dielectric bench test, a silicone elastomer sheet with relative permittivity 3.2 completely fills the 3.00 × 10⁻⁴ m gap between parallel metal plates of area 0.24 m² inside a industrial proximity-sensing pad. When the assembly is charged to 320 V (take ε₀ = 8.85 × 10⁻¹² F m⁻¹), calculate the energy stored per unit volume inside the dielectric.
items.workedSolution: Uniform field E = V / d = 320 / 0.0003 = 1.07 × 10⁶ V m⁻¹. Energy density u_E = ½εᵣε₀E² = 0.5 × 3.2 × 8.85 × 10⁻¹² × (1.07 × 10⁶)² = 16.1 J m⁻³.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates E = V/d and u_E = ½εᵣε₀E² to obtain 16.1 J m⁻³ (D).

items.stem: In a laboratory dielectric-constant cell, a regulated DC supply applies 150 V across two flat parallel electrodes of effective area 1.25 m² spaced 4.00 × 10⁻⁴ m apart. The space between the electrodes is filled uniformly by nylon spacer of relative permittivity 7.5 (ε₀ = 8.85 × 10⁻¹² F m⁻¹). What magnitude of charge is stored on each conducting plate?
items.workedSolution: Capacitance C = εᵣε₀A / d = 2.07 × 10⁻⁷ F. Plate charge Q = CV = 2.07 × 10⁻⁷ × 150 = 3.11 × 10⁻⁵ C.

markScheme.criterion: Combines C = εᵣε₀A/d with Q = CV to obtain 3.11 × 10⁻⁵ C (A).

items.stem: Within a polymer-film pulse energy storage cell, a uniform electric field is established across a 2.50 × 10⁻⁴ m layer of polypropylene film (εᵣ = 3.8) sandwiched between conducting plates of area 0.32 m² held at a potential difference of 320 V. Using ε₀ = 8.85 × 10⁻¹² F m⁻¹, calculate the energy stored per unit volume inside the dielectric.
items.workedSolution: Uniform field E = V / d = 320 / 0.00025 = 1.28 × 10⁶ V m⁻¹. Energy density u_E = ½εᵣε₀E² = 0.5 × 3.8 × 8.85 × 10⁻¹² × (1.28 × 10⁶)² = 27.5 J m⁻³.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates E = V/d and u_E = ½εᵣε₀E² to obtain 27.5 J m⁻³ (A).

items.stem: A medical defibrillator test capacitor consists of parallel conducting plates of overlapping area 0.6 m² separated by a uniform mica insulator layer of thickness 8.00 × 10⁻⁴ m and relative permittivity 5.2. A steady potential difference of 150 V is maintained across the plates (ε₀ = 8.85 × 10⁻¹² F m⁻¹). What electrostatic energy is stored in the capacitor?

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates C = εᵣε₀A/d and U = ½CV² to obtain 3.88 × 10⁻⁴ J (C).

items.stem: During a dielectric bench test, a polyimide sheet sheet with relative permittivity 4.4 completely fills the 2.00 × 10⁻⁴ m gap between parallel metal plates of area 0.48 m² inside a aerospace humidity-compensated sensor. When the assembly is charged to 320 V (take ε₀ = 8.85 × 10⁻¹² F m⁻¹), calculate the energy stored per unit volume inside the dielectric.
items.workedSolution: Uniform field E = V / d = 320 / 0.0002 = 1.60 × 10⁶ V m⁻¹. Energy density u_E = ½εᵣε₀E² = 0.5 × 4.4 × 8.85 × 10⁻¹² × (1.60 × 10⁶)² = 49.8 J m⁻³.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates E = V/d and u_E = ½εᵣε₀E² to obtain 49.8 J m⁻³ (A).

items.stem: To characterise silicone elastomer of relative permittivity 7.5, a industrial proximity-sensing pad with plate area 0.24 m² and plate spacing 4.00 × 10⁻⁴ m is energised by a 320 V DC source (ε₀ = 8.85 × 10⁻¹² F m⁻¹). calculate the capacitance of the dielectric-filled assembly.

markScheme.criterion: Applies C = εᵣε₀A / d to obtain 3.98 × 10⁻⁸ F (D).

items.stem: In a precision touch-panel sensing element, a regulated DC supply applies 150 V across two flat parallel electrodes of effective area 0.4 m² spaced 2.50 × 10⁻⁴ m apart. The space between the electrodes is filled uniformly by borosilicate glass of relative permittivity 3.8 (ε₀ = 8.85 × 10⁻¹² F m⁻¹). What magnitude of charge is stored on each conducting plate?
items.workedSolution: Capacitance C = εᵣε₀A / d = 5.38 × 10⁻⁸ F. Plate charge Q = CV = 5.38 × 10⁻⁸ × 150 = 8.07 × 10⁻⁶ C.

markScheme.criterion: Combines C = εᵣε₀A/d with Q = CV to obtain 8.07 × 10⁻⁶ C (A).

items.stem: Within a radio-frequency tuning plate assembly, a uniform electric field is established across a 8.00 × 10⁻⁴ m layer of polystyrene slab (εᵣ = 5.2) sandwiched between conducting plates of area 0.75 m² held at a potential difference of 320 V. Using ε₀ = 8.85 × 10⁻¹² F m⁻¹, calculate the energy stored per unit volume inside the dielectric.
items.workedSolution: Uniform field E = V / d = 320 / 0.0008 = 4.00 × 10⁵ V m⁻¹. Energy density u_E = ½εᵣε₀E² = 0.5 × 5.2 × 8.85 × 10⁻¹² × (4.00 × 10⁵)² = 3.68 J m⁻³.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates E = V/d and u_E = ½εᵣε₀E² to obtain 3.68 J m⁻³ (D).

items.stem: A laboratory dielectric-constant cell consists of parallel conducting plates of overlapping area 1.5 m² separated by a uniform nylon spacer layer of thickness 5.00 × 10⁻⁴ m and relative permittivity 6.8. A steady potential difference of 150 V is maintained across the plates (ε₀ = 8.85 × 10⁻¹² F m⁻¹). What electrostatic energy is stored in the capacitor?

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates C = εᵣε₀A/d and U = ½CV² to obtain 2.03 × 10⁻³ J (B).

items.stem: Parallel rectangular plates of area 0.32 m² in a polymer-film pulse energy storage cell enclose a solid polypropylene film slab (relative permittivity 3.2) that sets the plate separation at 3.00 × 10⁻⁴ m. Taking ε₀ = 8.85 × 10⁻¹² F m⁻¹ with an applied terminal voltage of 320 V, calculate the capacitance of the dielectric-filled assembly.

markScheme.criterion: Applies C = εᵣε₀A / d to obtain 3.02 × 10⁻⁸ F (C).

items.stem: A laboratory prototype of a medical defibrillator test capacitor employs parallel electrodes of area 0.75 m², a mica insulator dielectric of thickness 2.00 × 10⁻⁴ m and relative permittivity 4.4, and a charging supply of 150 V (ε₀ = 8.85 × 10⁻¹² F m⁻¹). What magnitude of charge is stored on each conducting plate?
items.workedSolution: Capacitance C = εᵣε₀A / d = 1.46 × 10⁻⁷ F. Plate charge Q = CV = 1.46 × 10⁻⁷ × 150 = 2.19 × 10⁻⁵ C.

markScheme.criterion: Combines C = εᵣε₀A/d with Q = CV to obtain 2.19 × 10⁻⁵ C (A).

items.stem: During a dielectric bench test, a fused quartz wafer sheet with relative permittivity 6 completely fills the 6.00 × 10⁻⁴ m gap between parallel metal plates of area 1.1 m² inside a microbalance displacement detector. When the assembly is charged to 320 V (take ε₀ = 8.85 × 10⁻¹² F m⁻¹), calculate the energy stored per unit volume inside the dielectric.
items.workedSolution: Uniform field E = V / d = 320 / 0.0006 = 5.33 × 10⁵ V m⁻¹. Energy density u_E = ½εᵣε₀E² = 0.5 × 6 × 8.85 × 10⁻¹² × (5.33 × 10⁵)² = 7.55 J m⁻³.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates E = V/d and u_E = ½εᵣε₀E² to obtain 7.55 J m⁻³ (B).

items.stem: A vacuum-insulated capacitive load cell has plate area 0.85 m², initial separation 2.40 × 10⁻⁴ m, and relative permittivity 5.5, energised initially at 280 V (ε₀ = 8.85 × 10⁻¹² F m⁻¹). Next, the assembly is kept connected across the DC source at constant potential difference while the plate separation is adjusted to 3.60 × 10⁻⁴ m with εᵣ = 5.5 throughout. What is the final electrostatic energy stored in the modified state?
items.workedSolution: Initial capacitance C = 1.72 × 10⁻⁷ F, modified capacitance C′ = 1.15 × 10⁻⁷ F. Under constant-voltage, final stored energy U′ = 4.51 × 10⁻³ J.

markScheme.criterion: Computes modified capacitance C′ and evaluates final stored energy 4.51 × 10⁻³ J (D).

items.stem: During calibration of a high-voltage plate-separation apparatus (ε₀ = 8.85 × 10⁻¹² F m⁻¹), a 100 V supply charges parallel electrodes of area 0.25 m² spaced 5.00 × 10⁻⁴ m apart with relative permittivity 3.5. The electrodes are disconnected from the DC source so the plates remain electrically isolated, and the plate separation is then adjusted to 0.001 m at unchanged relative permittivity 3.5. What is the signed change in stored electrostatic energy ΔU = U_final − U_initial?
items.workedSolution: Initial C = 1.55 × 10⁻⁸ F and U_i = ½CV² = 7.74 × 10⁻⁵ J. Modified C′ = 7.74 × 10⁻⁹ F gives U_f = 1.55 × 10⁻⁴ J, so ΔU = U_f − U_i = 7.74 × 10⁻⁵ J.

markScheme.criterion: Determines U_i and U_f under the isolated-charge constraint to obtain ΔU = 7.74 × 10⁻⁵ J (B).

items.stem: Parallel electrodes of area 0.45 m² in a piezo-positioned capacitor stage enclose a medium of relative permittivity 4.8 across an initial gap of 3.00 × 10⁻⁴ m at 220 V (ε₀ = 8.85 × 10⁻¹² F m⁻¹). Subsequently, the device is kept connected across the DC source at constant potential difference while the plate separation is adjusted to 7.50 × 10⁻⁴ m with the same εᵣ = 4.8. What is the final electrostatic energy stored in the modified state?
items.workedSolution: Initial capacitance C = 6.37 × 10⁻⁸ F, modified capacitance C′ = 2.55 × 10⁻⁸ F. Under constant-voltage, final stored energy U′ = 6.17 × 10⁻⁴ J.

markScheme.criterion: Computes modified capacitance C′ and evaluates final stored energy 6.17 × 10⁻⁴ J (B).

items.stem: An experimental capacitive MEMS accelerometer features plates of area 0.7 m² at initial spacing 6.00 × 10⁻⁴ m filled with a medium of relative permittivity 6.5 and charged to 420 V (take ε₀ = 8.85 × 10⁻¹² F m⁻¹). The plates are disconnected from the DC source so the plates remain electrically isolated, and the plate separation is then adjusted to 3.00 × 10⁻⁴ m while εᵣ stays at 6.5. What is the new potential difference across the isolated plates?
items.workedSolution: For isolated plates, charge Q is conserved while C′ = C₀(d/d′). Therefore V′ = Q / C′ = V₀(d′/d) = 420 × (0.0003 / 0.0006) = 210 V.

markScheme.criterion: Uses charge conservation V′ = V₀(d′/d) to obtain 210 V (B).

items.stem: Charged initially to 180 V, a variable-gap precision electrometer with plate area 1 m², gap 4.00 × 10⁻⁴ m, and relative permittivity 4 is kept connected across the DC source at constant potential difference while the plate separation is adjusted to 6.00 × 10⁻⁴ m (εᵣ = 4, ε₀ = 8.85 × 10⁻¹² F m⁻¹). What is the signed change in stored electrostatic energy ΔU = U_final − U_initial?
items.workedSolution: Initial C = 8.85 × 10⁻⁸ F and U_i = ½CV² = 1.43 × 10⁻³ J. Modified C′ = 5.90 × 10⁻⁸ F gives U_f = 9.56 × 10⁻⁴ J, so ΔU = U_f − U_i = −4.78 × 10⁻⁴ J.

markScheme.criterion: Determines U_i and U_f under the constant-voltage constraint to obtain ΔU = −4.78 × 10⁻⁴ J (C).

items.stem: In a dielectric displacement gauge, parallel plates of area 0.35 m² separated by 2.40 × 10⁻⁴ m with dielectric relative permittivity 5.5 are initially charged to 350 V (take ε₀ = 8.85 × 10⁻¹² F m⁻¹). The capacitor is disconnected from the DC source so the plates remain electrically isolated, and the plate separation is then adjusted to 4.80 × 10⁻⁴ m (maintaining relative permittivity 5.5). What is the final electrostatic energy stored in the modified state?
items.workedSolution: Initial capacitance C = 7.10 × 10⁻⁸ F, modified capacitance C′ = 3.55 × 10⁻⁸ F. Under isolated-charge, final stored energy U′ = 8.70 × 10⁻³ J.

markScheme.criterion: Computes modified capacitance C′ and evaluates final stored energy 8.70 × 10⁻³ J (C).

items.stem: A electrostatic actuator test rig has plate area 0.55 m², initial separation 5.00 × 10⁻⁴ m, and relative permittivity 3.5, energised initially at 140 V (ε₀ = 8.85 × 10⁻¹² F m⁻¹). Next, the assembly is kept connected across the DC source at constant potential difference while the plate separation is adjusted to 0.00125 m with εᵣ = 3.5 throughout. What is the final electrostatic energy stored in the modified state?
items.workedSolution: Initial capacitance C = 3.41 × 10⁻⁸ F, modified capacitance C′ = 1.36 × 10⁻⁸ F. Under constant-voltage, final stored energy U′ = 1.34 × 10⁻⁴ J.

markScheme.criterion: Computes modified capacitance C′ and evaluates final stored energy 1.34 × 10⁻⁴ J (C).

items.stem: In a biomedical amplifier coupling network, parallel branches containing C_p1 = 10 μF and C_p2 = 20 μF are wired in series with capacitor C_s = 30 μF and charged by a steady 7 V source. What is the equivalent capacitance of the complete three-capacitor network?
items.workedSolution: Parallel bank C_p = 10 + 20 = 30 μF. Combining in series with C_s = 30 μF gives C_eq = (C_s C_p)/(C_s + C_p) = 1.50 × 10⁻⁵ F.

markScheme.criterion: Finds C_p = 30 μF and combines in series with C_s to obtain 1.50 × 10⁻⁵ F (B).

items.stem: Two capacitors rated C₁ = 12 μF and C₂ = 36 μF are wired end-to-end in series across an ideal 17 V terminal supply on a DC rail smoothing subcircuit. What potential difference is developed across capacitor C₁?
items.workedSolution: Equivalent capacitance C_eq = 9.00 × 10⁻⁶ F, so series charge Q = C_eq V₀ = 1.53 × 10⁻⁴ C. Across C₁, V₁ = Q / C₁ = 12.8 V.

markScheme.criterion: Finds common series charge Q and computes V₁ = Q/C₁ = 12.8 V (A).

items.stem: During testing of a camera strobe flash bank, an engineer connects uncharged capacitors C₁ = 12 μF and C₂ = 24 μF in series with a steady 43 V cell. What total electrostatic energy is stored in the two-capacitor series combination?

items.stem: A pulsed-power laboratory network uses a capacitor C_s = 60 μF connected in series with a parallel bank formed by C_p1 = 12 μF and C_p2 = 18 μF across a 13 V DC supply. What is the equivalent capacitance of the complete three-capacitor network?
items.workedSolution: Parallel bank C_p = 12 + 18 = 30 μF. Combining in series with C_s = 60 μF gives C_eq = (C_s C_p)/(C_s + C_p) = 2.00 × 10⁻⁵ F.

markScheme.criterion: Finds C_p = 30 μF and combines in series with C_s to obtain 2.00 × 10⁻⁵ F (A).

items.stem: Across a regulated 23 V rail in a avionics backup energy module, capacitor C₁ (15 μF) is placed in series with capacitor C₂ (30 μF). What is the total equivalent capacitance of the series pair?
items.workedSolution: For series capacitors, 1/C_eq = 1/C₁ + 1/C₂, giving C_eq = (15 × 30)/(15 + 30) μF = 1.00 × 10⁻⁵ F.

items.stem: When switch S closes in a industrial watchdog reset timer, a 25 μF uncharged capacitor charges from a 18 V cell through a 4 kΩ resistor over an interval of 0.09 s. How much electrostatic energy is stored in the capacitor at t = 0.09 s?
items.workedSolution: τ = RC = 0.100 s, giving V_C(0.09 s) = 10.7 V. Stored energy U = ½CV_C² = 0.5 × 2.50 × 10⁻⁵ × (10.7)² = 1.43 × 10⁻³ J.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates V_C(t) and computes U(t) = ½CV_C(t)² = 1.43 × 10⁻³ J (D).

options.label: C

items.stem: A 20 μF capacitor at 18 V in a heart-pacemaker timing circuit discharges exponentially through a series resistance of 15 kΩ; measurements are recorded 0.27 s after closing the switch. What is the potential difference across the capacitor at t = 0.27 s?
items.workedSolution: Time constant τ = RC = 0.300 s. For discharging, V_C(0.27 s) = 18 e^(−0.27/0.300) = 7.32 V.

markScheme.criterion: Finds τ = RC and evaluates V_C at t = 0.27 s to obtain 7.32 V (B).

items.stem: In a oscilloscope RC time-constant practical, a 120 μF capacitor initially charged to 9 V begins discharging through a 2.5 kΩ resistor when switch S closes, and a sensor samples the circuit after 0.45 s. What is the current in the resistor at t = 0.45 s?
items.workedSolution: Initial current I₀ = V₀ / R = 9 / 2500 = 3.60 × 10⁻³ A. With τ = RC = 0.300 s, I(t) = I₀ e^(−t/τ) = 8.03 × 10⁻⁴ A.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Stops at the initial peak current I₀ = V₀/R without applying exponential decay e^(−t/RC).

items.stem: During field ramping in a wireless inductive telemetry receiver coil (240 turns, area 0.02 m², resistance 16 Ω), a uniform magnetic field directed at an angle of 20° with the normal to the coil ramps uniformly from 0.36 T to 1.08 T over 0.05 s. What is the magnitude of the average emf induced in the coil?
items.workedSolution: Angle to normal θ_n = 20°. |Δ(NΦ)| = 240 × |1.08 − 0.36| × 0.02 × cos 20° = 3.25 Wb. Average |ε| = |Δ(NΦ)| / Δt = 65.0 V.

markScheme.criterion: Projects flux along coil normal (20°) and evaluates |ε| = N|ΔΦ|/Δt = 65.0 V (C).

items.stem: Fixed so that a uniform magnetic field forms an angle of 35° with the plane of the coil, a closed rotary position-sensing pickup winding of 300 turns, area 0.005 m², and resistance 5 Ω experiences a field that decays uniformly from 0.56 T to zero in 0.1 s. What average induced current circulates around the closed coil during the ramp?
items.workedSolution: With θ_normal = 55°, |ε| = N|ΔB|A cos 55° / Δt = 4.82 V. Average current I = |ε| / R = 4.82 / 5 = 0.964 A.

markScheme.criterion: Computes |ε| using θ_normal = 55° and I = |ε|/R = 0.964 A (D).

items.stem: In a plasma-tokamak diagnostic flux loop, a flat winding of 400 turns, area 0.016 m², and circuit resistance 16 Ω sits in a magnetic field inclined at an angle of 65° with the normal to the coil. The magnetic flux density ramps uniformly from 0.22 T to 0.55 T over 0.025 s. What is the initial magnetic flux linkage NΦ₁ of the coil?
items.workedSolution: Angle to coil normal θ_n = 65°. Initial flux linkage NΦ₁ = NBA cos θ_n = 400 × 0.22 × 0.016 × cos 65° = 0.595 Wb.

markScheme.criterion: Uses θ_normal = 65° in NΦ₁ = NBA cos θ_normal to obtain 0.595 Wb (C).

items.stem: Connected to a charge integrator of total loop resistance 2 Ω, a flat earth-inductor compass loop containing 140 turns of area 0.022 m² faces normal to a field that reverses from +0.12 T to −0.120 T in 0.2 s. What total magnitude of electric charge ΔQ flows around the circuit during this reversal?

items.stem: A uniform 1.25 T magnetic field directed out of the page permeates a levitated glider regenerator bench whose smooth conducting rails sit 0.32 m apart across a 2.4 Ω external resistor. An external agent pulls a rod of resistance 1 Ω to the right at constant speed 8 m s⁻¹. What is the terminal potential difference across the external load resistor?

markScheme.criterion: Uses V_term = BLv × R/(R + r) to obtain 2.26 V (C).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Inverts the potential-divider ratio as ε(R + r)/R instead of εR/(R + r).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Calculates the lost volts I r inside the moving rod instead of V_term = I R across the load.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Reports the full motional emf BLv and ignores the internal potential drop I r across the moving rod.

items.stem: In a electromagnetic rail-braking demonstrator, parallel rails of separation 0.5 m are closed by a 4.2 Ω resistor inside a perpendicular 0.45 T magnetic field (directed into the page). A metal rod of resistance 1.2 Ω moves steadily to the right at 4 m s⁻¹. What mechanical power must be supplied to keep the rod moving at constant speed?
items.workedSolution: ε = BLv = 0.900 V; R_tot = 4.2 + 1.2 = 5.4 Ω. Mechanical input power equals total Joule heating P = ε² / R_tot = 0.150 W.

items.stem: Travelling to the left at constant velocity 8 m s⁻¹, a crossbar of resistance 0.4 Ω spans frictionless rails 0.2 m apart on a linear regenerator test track connected to a 1.4 Ω load in a 0.9 T field (directed out of the page). What induced current circulates around the closed loop?
items.workedSolution: Motional emf ε = BLv = 0.9 × 0.2 × 8 = 1.44 V. Loop current I = ε / (R + r) = 1.44 / 1.8 = 0.800 A.

options.label: C

items.stem: Within a magnetohydrodynamic copper-bar carriage, a 2.4 Ω load terminates smooth rails separated by 0.32 m in a uniform 0.25 T field directed into the page, while a sliding rod (resistance 0.6 Ω) is driven to the right at 4 m s⁻¹. What external pulling force magnitude is needed to maintain this constant speed?
items.workedSolution: Motional emf ε = BLv = 0.320 V. Total loop resistance R_tot = 2.4 + 0.6 = 3 Ω, giving I = ε / R_tot = 0.107 A. Pulling force F = BIL = 8.53 × 10⁻³ N.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates ε = BLv, I = ε/(R + r), and F = BIL = 8.53 × 10⁻³ N (A).

options.distractorRationale: Neglects the internal resistance of the moving rod and divides by the external load resistance R alone.

options.distractorRationale: Stops after evaluating the induced loop current I = BLv/(R + r) without multiplying by B L.

items.stem: During a steady-state run on a frictionless laboratory induction sled, a conducting rod of resistance 0.8 Ω glides right at 8 m s⁻¹ across rails 0.5 m apart bridged by 4.2 Ω in a 0.6 T magnetic field (directed out of the page). What is the terminal potential difference across the external load resistor?
items.workedSolution: ε = BLv = 2.40 V; loop current I = ε / (R + r) = 0.480 A. Terminal p.d. across load V_term = I R = 0.480 × 4.2 = 2.02 V.

markScheme.criterion: Uses V_term = BLv × R/(R + r) to obtain 2.02 V (C).

options.distractorRationale: Reports the full motional emf BLv and ignores the internal potential drop I r across the moving rod.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Inverts the potential-divider ratio as ε(R + r)/R instead of εR/(R + r).

options.label: D

items.stem: On a drop-tower eddy-braking crossbar, a conducting bar of internal resistance 1 Ω slides to the left at a steady speed of 4 m s⁻¹ along parallel horizontal rails of negligible resistance spaced 0.2 m apart. A uniform 1.1 T magnetic field (directed into the page) threads the rails, which are bridged by a 1.4 Ω load resistor. What mechanical power must be supplied to keep the rod moving at constant speed?
items.workedSolution: ε = BLv = 0.880 V; R_tot = 1.4 + 1 = 2.4 Ω. Mechanical input power equals total Joule heating P = ε² / R_tot = 0.323 W.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Uses ε²/R and neglects the rod resistance r when finding loop current.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Evaluates magnetic braking force BIL without multiplying by speed v.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Calculates only the power dissipated in the external load I²R, omitting heating I²r inside the rod.

items.stem: A uniform 0.35 T magnetic field directed out of the page permeates a space-tether electrodynamic rail rig whose smooth conducting rails sit 0.32 m apart across a 2.4 Ω external resistor. An external agent pulls a rod of resistance 1.2 Ω to the right at constant speed 8 m s⁻¹. What induced current circulates around the closed loop?
items.workedSolution: Motional emf ε = BLv = 0.35 × 0.32 × 8 = 0.896 V. Loop current I = ε / (R + r) = 0.896 / 3.6 = 0.249 A.

items.stem: In a wind-turbine test generator driving a load bank, a winding of 220 turns and cross-sectional area 0.025 m² revolves at 50 Hz within a 0.16 T field and supplies sinusoidal AC directly to a 80 Ω resistive load. What is the root-mean-square (rms) potential difference across the load?
items.workedSolution: Peak emf ε₀ = 2πfNBA = 2π(50)(220)(0.16)(0.025) = 276 V. Therefore V_rms = ε₀ / √2 = 195 V.

markScheme.criterion: Finds ε₀ = 2πfNBA and divides by √2 to obtain 195 V (D).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Multiplies peak emf ε₀ by √2 instead of dividing by √2.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Stops at peak emf ε₀ = 2πfNBA without dividing by √2.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Divides peak emf ε₀ by 2 (confusing the ½ power factor with the 1/√2 rms voltage factor).

items.stem: During load testing on a wind-turbine test generator driving a load bank, an ideal rotor coil (220 turns, area 0.025 m²) turns at 60 Hz in a uniform 0.3 T field while connected to a 80 Ω resistor. What is the root-mean-square (rms) potential difference across the load?
items.workedSolution: Peak emf ε₀ = 2πfNBA = 2π(60)(220)(0.3)(0.025) = 622 V. Therefore V_rms = ε₀ / √2 = 440 V.

markScheme.criterion: Finds ε₀ = 2πfNBA and divides by √2 to obtain 440 V (C).

options.label: D

items.stem: Connected via slip rings to a 12 Ω load in a aircraft auxiliary AC bus resistive test rig, an ideal coil of 60 turns and area 0.012 m² rotates at 80 Hz in a uniform 0.48 T magnetic field. What root-mean-square (rms) current flows through the load resistor?
items.workedSolution: ε₀ = 2πfNBA = 174 V, so V_rms = ε₀ / √2 = 123 V. Load rms current I_rms = V_rms / R = 123 / 12 = 10.2 A.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Omits the 2π factor when converting frequency f into angular speed ω = 2πf.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Calculates peak current I₀ = ε₀/R and omits dividing by √2 for rms current.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Divides peak current I₀ by 2 instead of √2.

items.stem: A laboratory slip-ring alternator with ohmic load uses a coil of negligible internal resistance with 140 turns and area 0.025 m² spinning at 25 Hz in a uniform 0.22 T magnetic field across a 25 Ω resistor. What mean electrical power is dissipated in the resistive load over a complete cycle?
items.workedSolution: Peak emf ε₀ = 2πfNBA = 121 V; V_rms = ε₀ / √2 = 85.5 V. Mean resistive power P_mean = V_rms² / R = ½ ε₀² / R = 293 W.

markScheme.criterion: Computes ε₀ = 2πfNBA and mean power P_mean = ½ε₀²/R = 293 W (C).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Divides V₀ by 2 instead of √2 before squaring in V_rms²/R, introducing a ¼ factor.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Calculates peak instantaneous power V₀²/R without applying the ½ sinusoidal average factor.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Divides peak power V₀I₀ by √2 instead of 2, forgetting that both V_rms = V₀/√2 and I_rms = I₀/√2 contribute a 1/√2 factor.

items.stem: Connected to a 500 V rms AC mains line, a laboratory bench variac step-down core (1600 primary turns, 320 secondary turns, efficiency 0.95 or 95%) feeds a pure 32 Ω resistor across its secondary winding. What is the rms potential difference induced across the secondary winding?
items.workedSolution: Using V_s / V_p = N_s / N_p gives V_s = 500 × (320 / 1600) = 100 V.

items.stem: In a substation distribution transformer having primary winding N_p = 400 and secondary winding N_s = 800, a 110 V rms input drives a 8 Ω secondary load at overall power efficiency η = 0.8 (80%). What mean thermal power is wasted in the transformer core and windings?
items.workedSolution: V_s = 220 V; P_out = V_s² / R_L = 6.05 × 10³ W. Input power P_in = P_out / η = 7.56 × 10³ W, so power loss P_loss = P_in − P_out = 1.51 × 10³ W.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates P_in = P_out/η and P_loss = P_in − P_out = 1.51 × 10³ W (D).

items.stem: During thermal-loss testing of a rack-mounted server isolation-stepdown unit, a 120 V rms primary supply energises 800 primary turns coupled to 40 secondary turns across a 24 Ω load with efficiency η = 0.88 (88%). What rms current is drawn from the primary AC supply?
items.workedSolution: Secondary rms voltage V_s = V_p(N_s/N_p) = 120(40/800) = 6.00 V. Output power P_out = V_s² / R_L = 1.50 W. Input power P_in = P_out / η = 1.70 W, so I_p = P_in / V_p = 0.0142 A.

markScheme.criterion: Computes V_s, P_out, and I_p = P_out / (η V_p) = 0.0142 A (D).

items.stem: Across a 6 Ω secondary load, a hospital X-ray filament supply transformer (1200 primary turns, 240 secondary turns) transfers AC power from a 200 V rms source at efficiency 0.92 (92%). What is the rms potential difference induced across the secondary winding?
items.workedSolution: Using V_s / V_p = N_s / N_p gives V_s = 200 × (240 / 1200) = 40.0 V.

items.stem: Operating at η = 0.96 (96%) efficiency from a 230 V rms AC source, a laminated-core arc-welding laminated-core transformer has N_p = 300 turns, N_s = 600 turns, and a 16 Ω secondary load resistor. What mean thermal power is wasted in the transformer core and windings?
items.workedSolution: V_s = 460 V; P_out = V_s² / R_L = 1.32 × 10⁴ W. Input power P_in = P_out / η = 1.38 × 10⁴ W, so power loss P_loss = P_in − P_out = 551 W.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates P_in = P_out/η and P_loss = P_in − P_out = 551 W (B).

items.stem: A railway signalling trackside transformer with 500 primary turns and 25 secondary turns operates at an efficiency of 0.85 (85%) from a 240 V rms AC supply while driving a 48 Ω resistive secondary load. What rms current is drawn from the primary AC supply?
items.workedSolution: Secondary rms voltage V_s = V_p(N_s/N_p) = 240(25/500) = 12.0 V. Output power P_out = V_s² / R_L = 3.00 W. Input power P_in = P_out / η = 3.53 W, so I_p = P_in / V_p = 0.0147 A.

markScheme.criterion: Computes V_s, P_out, and I_p = P_out / (η V_p) = 0.0147 A (B).

items.stem: In a time-of-flight ion-beam steerer, a proton (charge +1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C, mass 1.67 × 10⁻²⁷ kg) enters horizontally at 5.80 × 10⁵ m s⁻¹ along the midplane between parallel deflecting plates of length 0.05 m and separation 0.04 m maintained at 1390 V (neglecting gravity). What is the angular deflection θ (in degrees) of the particle velocity as it leaves the plates?
items.workedSolution: |v_y| = a_y t = (|q|V / md)(L / v₀) = 2.87 × 10⁵ m s⁻¹. Therefore θ = arctan(|v_y| / v₀) = 26.3°.

items.stem: Travelling at an initial horizontal speed of 1.80 × 10⁷ m s⁻¹, a electron (q = −1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C, m = 9.11 × 10⁻³¹ kg) passes centrally between parallel plates of length 0.06 m spaced 0.06 m apart across a 1370 V potential difference in a electron-beam lithography electrostatic deflector. What is the resultant speed of the particle as it emerges from the plates?
items.workedSolution: Exit transverse speed |v_y| = (|q|VL)/(md v₀) = 1.34 × 10⁷ m s⁻¹. Resultant speed v_exit = √(v₀² + v_y²) = 2.24 × 10⁷ m s⁻¹.

items.stem: Parallel plates of length 0.075 m and gap 0.05 m in a vacuum beam-diagnostics parallel-plate cell are held at 230 V. A proton of charge +1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C and mass 1.67 × 10⁻²⁷ kg enters midway between the plates parallel to their surfaces at 3.00 × 10⁵ m s⁻¹. What is the magnitude of the transverse deflection as the particle exits the plates?
items.workedSolution: Transit time t = L / v₀ = 0.075 / 3.00 × 10⁵ = 2.50 × 10⁻⁷ s. Transverse acceleration a_y = |q|V / (md) = 4.41 × 10¹¹ m s⁻². Deflection |Δy| = ½ a_y t² = 0.0138 m.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates t = L/v₀, a_y = |q|V/(md), and |Δy| = ½a_y t² = 0.0138 m (C).

items.stem: During calibration of a electrostatic particle-beam chopper, a collimated electron beam (charge −1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C, mass 9.11 × 10⁻³¹ kg) enters at 2.00 × 10⁷ m s⁻¹ along the central axis of 0.08 m long parallel electrodes separated by 0.04 m at p.d. 387 V. What is the angular deflection θ (in degrees) of the particle velocity as it leaves the plates?
items.workedSolution: |v_y| = a_y t = (|q|V / md)(L / v₀) = 6.80 × 10⁶ m s⁻¹. Therefore θ = arctan(|v_y| / v₀) = 18.8°.

items.stem: Within a vacuum accelerator monochromatic ion collimator, a proton (+1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C, 1.67 × 10⁻²⁷ kg) is injected horizontally to the right at 1.50 × 10⁵ m s⁻¹ between plates 0.015 m apart at p.d. 750 V (upper plate negative) inside a perpendicular 0.2 T field (out of the page). What is the initial upward transverse acceleration of the proton upon entering the crossed fields?
items.workedSolution: E = V/d = 5.00 × 10⁴ V m⁻¹. Upward electric force F_E = qE = 8.00 × 10⁻¹⁵ N; downward magnetic force |F_B| = qvB = 4.80 × 10⁻¹⁵ N. Net upward acceleration a_y = (F_E − |F_B|) / m = 1.92 × 10¹² m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts opposing qvB from qE and divides by m to obtain 1.92 × 10¹² m s⁻² (D).

items.stem: During tuning of a accelerator-mass-spectrometry pre-filter (180 V across a 0.03 m gap, upper plate positive, with B = 0.32 T into the page), a proton of charge +1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C and mass 1.67 × 10⁻²⁷ kg is injected horizontally along the central axis. At what speed must the proton travel to pass straight through the exit slit undeflected?
items.workedSolution: Uniform electric field E = V / d = 180 / 0.03 = 6.00 × 10³ V m⁻¹. Zero net deflection requires qE = qvB, so v_sel = E / B = V / (Bd) = 1.88 × 10⁴ m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Uses v_sel = V / (Bd) to obtain 1.88 × 10⁴ m s⁻¹ (B).

items.stem: In a electron-microscope Wien monochromator, parallel plates separated by 0.02 m are held at 320 V (upper plate negative) perpendicular to a uniform 0.12 T magnetic field (out of the page). A proton (charge +1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C, mass 1.67 × 10⁻²⁷ kg) is injected horizontally to the right at 8.00 × 10⁴ m s⁻¹. At what speed would a proton instead have to enter this same selector to pass straight through undeflected?
items.workedSolution: Electric field E = V / d = 320 / 0.02 = 1.60 × 10⁴ V m⁻¹. Undeflected transmission requires qvB = qE, giving v_sel = E / B = 1.33 × 10⁵ m s⁻¹.

items.stem: A plasma neutral-beam ion velocity selector combines parallel electrodes 0.04 m apart at 600 V (upper plate positive) with a crossed 0.2 T magnetic field (into the page) for protons (q = +1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C, m = 1.67 × 10⁻²⁷ kg) injected horizontally along the central axis. At what speed must the proton travel to pass straight through the exit slit undeflected?
items.workedSolution: Uniform electric field E = V / d = 600 / 0.04 = 1.50 × 10⁴ V m⁻¹. Zero net deflection requires qE = qvB, so v_sel = E / B = V / (Bd) = 7.50 × 10⁴ m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Uses v_sel = V / (Bd) to obtain 7.50 × 10⁴ m s⁻¹ (D).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Multiplies E by B instead of dividing E / B in the balanced-force condition qE = qvB.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Multiplies V by d instead of dividing V by d when finding electric field E = V/d.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Inverts v = E/B and computes B/E = Bd/V instead of V/(Bd).

items.stem: Crossed fields in a atomic-physics crossed-E/B beam gate are produced by 900 V across plates spaced 0.025 m apart (upper plate negative) and a 0.32 T field directed out of the page; a proton (+1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C, 1.67 × 10⁻²⁷ kg) is injected horizontally to the right at 6.75 × 10⁴ m s⁻¹. What is the initial upward transverse acceleration of the proton upon entering the crossed fields?
items.workedSolution: E = V/d = 3.60 × 10⁴ V m⁻¹. Upward electric force F_E = qE = 5.76 × 10⁻¹⁵ N; downward magnetic force |F_B| = qvB = 3.46 × 10⁻¹⁵ N. Net upward acceleration a_y = (F_E − |F_B|) / m = 1.38 × 10¹² m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts opposing qvB from qE and divides by m to obtain 1.38 × 10¹² m s⁻² (B).

items.stem: Within a vacuum Wien crossed-field velocity filter, a proton (+1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C, 1.67 × 10⁻²⁷ kg) is injected horizontally along the central axis between plates 0.015 m apart at p.d. 240 V (upper plate positive) inside a perpendicular 0.12 T field (into the page). At what speed must the proton travel to pass straight through the exit slit undeflected?
items.workedSolution: Uniform electric field E = V / d = 240 / 0.015 = 1.60 × 10⁴ V m⁻¹. Zero net deflection requires qE = qvB, so v_sel = E / B = V / (Bd) = 1.33 × 10⁵ m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Uses v_sel = V / (Bd) to obtain 1.33 × 10⁵ m s⁻¹ (B).

items.stem: In a nuclear-forensics Bainbridge analyser, two chlorine isotopes of equal charge +1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C and masses m₁ = 5.81 × 10⁻²⁶ kg and m₂ = 6.14 × 10⁻²⁶ kg pass undeflected through a velocity selector (E = 6.80 × 10⁴ V m⁻¹, B₁ = 0.35 T) before entering a semicircular analyser chamber with uniform field B₂ = 0.7 T (out of the page). What is the orbital radius r₁ of the lighter isotope inside the deflection chamber?
items.workedSolution: Selector speed v = E / B₁ = 1.94 × 10⁵ m s⁻¹. In chamber field B₂, r₁ = m₁v / (qB₂) = m₁E / (qB₁B₂) = 0.101 m.

options.label: A

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Confuses orbital radius r₁ with semicircular impact diameter D₁ = 2r₁.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Divides E by B₂ instead of B₁ in the velocity selector, evaluating m₁E/(qB₂²).

items.stem: A planetary-probe isotopic magnetic sector filters potassium ions (charge +1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C, masses m₁ = 6.47 × 10⁻²⁶ kg and m₂ = 6.81 × 10⁻²⁶ kg) using crossed fields E = 9.60 × 10⁴ V m⁻¹ and B₁ = 0.25 T, then bends them through semicircular arcs onto a detector plate in a chamber field B₂ = 0.6 T (into the page). How far from the entry slit S does the lighter isotope strike the detector wall?
items.workedSolution: v = E / B₁ = 3.84 × 10⁵ m s⁻¹ and r₁ = m₁v / (qB₂) = 0.259 m. Strike distance from slit S is D₁ = 2r₁ = 0.518 m.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Reports the orbital radius r₁ rather than the semicircular chord distance D₁ = 2r₁ from slit S.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Uses B₁² instead of B₁B₂ in D₁ = 2m₁E/(qB₁B₂).

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Calculates the separation ΔD between the two isotopes rather than the slit-to-impact distance 2r₁.

items.stem: Ions of two carbon isotopes carrying charge +1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C (m₁ = 1.99 × 10⁻²⁶ kg, m₂ = 2.32 × 10⁻²⁶ kg) emerge from the E = 4.00 × 10⁴ V m⁻¹, B₁ = 0.35 T selector of a environmental tracer Bainbridge instrument into a perpendicular B₂ = 0.7 T deflection chamber (out of the page). What is the straight-line separation ΔD between the two isotope strike marks on the detector wall?
items.workedSolution: Selected speed v = E / B₁ = 1.14 × 10⁵ m s⁻¹. Semicircular strike separation ΔD = 2(r₂ − r₁) = 2(m₂ − m₁)E / (q B₁ B₂) = 6.73 × 10⁻³ m.

options.label: A

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Calculates the difference in orbital radii |r₂ − r₁| and forgets the factor of 2 for semicircular impact diameters ΔD = 2|r₂ − r₁|.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Reports the semicircular strike distance 2r₁ of the lighter isotope rather than the separation between isotopes.

items.stem: Within a high-resolution velocity-selected mass spectrograph, crossed selector fields E = 6.80 × 10⁴ V m⁻¹ and B₁ = 0.25 T admit neon isotopes of charge +1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C and masses m₁ = 3.32 × 10⁻²⁶ kg and m₂ = 3.65 × 10⁻²⁶ kg through slit S into a uniform B₂ = 0.6 T magnetic sector (into the page). What is the orbital radius r₁ of the lighter isotope inside the deflection chamber?
items.workedSolution: Selector speed v = E / B₁ = 2.72 × 10⁵ m s⁻¹. In chamber field B₂, r₁ = m₁v / (qB₂) = m₁E / (qB₁B₂) = 0.0941 m.

items.stem: During isotopic analysis on a cosmochemistry meteorite isotope separator, magnesium ions (q = +3.20 × 10⁻¹⁹ C, m₁ = 3.98 × 10⁻²⁶ kg, m₂ = 4.32 × 10⁻²⁶ kg) traverse a velocity selector with E = 9.60 × 10⁴ V m⁻¹ and B₁ = 0.35 T and strike a photographic detector wall after semicircular deflection in B₂ = 0.7 T (out of the page). items.workedSolution: v = E / B₁ = 2.74 × 10⁵ m s⁻¹ and r₁ = m₁v / (qB₂) = 0.0487 m. Strike distance from slit S is D₁ = 2r₁ = 0.0975 m.

parts.prompt: Calculate the motional emf induced across the sliding rod.
Determine the induced current circulating around the rails.
Calculate the external pulling force magnitude required to maintain constant speed.

items.stem: Travelling to the left at constant velocity 8 m s⁻¹, a crossbar of resistance 0.6 Ω spans frictionless rails 0.2 m apart on a electromagnetic rail-braking demonstrator connected to a 1.4 Ω load in a 1.25 T field (directed out of the page).

markScheme.criterion: Divides ε from (a) by total loop resistance R + r.
Equates applied force to magnetic braking force F = BIL.

parts.prompt: Calculate the motional emf induced across the sliding rod.
Determine the induced current circulating around the rails.
Calculate the external pulling force magnitude required to maintain constant speed.

items.stem: Within a linear regenerator test track, a 2.4 Ω load terminates smooth rails separated by 0.32 m in a uniform 0.45 T field directed into the page, while a sliding rod (resistance 0.8 Ω) is driven to the right at 4 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Divides ε from (a) by total loop resistance R + r.
Equates applied force to magnetic braking force F = BIL.

parts.prompt: Calculate the motional emf induced across the sliding rod.
Determine the induced current circulating around the rails.
Calculate the external pulling force magnitude required to maintain constant speed.

items.stem: Travelling to the left at constant velocity 8 m s⁻¹, a crossbar of resistance 0.8 Ω spans frictionless rails 0.2 m apart on a levitated glider regenerator bench connected to a 1.4 Ω load in a 0.35 T field (directed out of the page).

markScheme.criterion: Divides ε from (a) by total loop resistance R + r.
Equates applied force to magnetic braking force F = BIL.

parts.prompt: Calculate the motional emf induced across the sliding rod.
Determine the induced current circulating around the rails.
Calculate the external pulling force magnitude required to maintain constant speed.

items.stem: Within a electromagnetic rail-braking demonstrator, a 2.4 Ω load terminates smooth rails separated by 0.32 m in a uniform 0.75 T field directed into the page, while a sliding rod (resistance 1 Ω) is driven to the right at 4 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Divides ε from (a) by total loop resistance R + r.
Equates applied force to magnetic braking force F = BIL.

parts.prompt: Calculate the electric field magnitude E between the parallel plates.
Calculate the speed v_sel required for the proton to pass straight through undeflected.

items.stem: Within a vacuum atomic-physics crossed-E/B beam gate, a proton (+1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C, 1.67 × 10⁻²⁷ kg) is injected horizontally to the right at 7.50 × 10⁴ m s⁻¹ between plates 0.015 m apart at p.d. 600 V (upper plate negative) inside a perpendicular 0.32 T field (out of the page).

markScheme.criterion: Equates qE = qvB to obtain v_sel = E / B.
